# a--icon.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/primitives/a--icon.mdx

title: 'Icon (a--icon)'
navtitle: 'a--icon'
description: 'a--icon is a class for displaying icon elements.'

import { Container, Columns, Grid, Stack, Flex, Spacer, Cluster, Icon, Center } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { Cat, SmileyIcon } from "@phosphor-icons/react";
import {phIcons, logoIcons} from 'lism-css/react/atomic/Icon/presets';
import { Home } from 'lucide-react';

export const PresetIcons = ({icons}) => {
  return <Grid layout="autoColumns" cols="10rem" g="15">
      {Object.keys(icons).map((iconName) => {
        return (
          <Stack key={iconName} g="10" ai="center" bgc="base-2" bdrs="10" p="15">
            <Icon icon={iconName} fz="xl" />
            <span class="u--trim -fz:xs -ff:mono -d:b">{iconName}</span>
          </Stack>
        );
      })}
  </Grid>;
}

`a--icon` is a class for displaying icon elements.

## CSS

<SrcCode path="src/scss/primitives/atomic/_icon.scss" />

## Lism Component

`<Icon>` automatically adds `aria-label` and `role="img"` when `label` is specified, or `aria-hidden="true"` when it is not.

### Import

<ImportPackage component="Icon" />

### HTML Structure

```pug
svg.a--icon[aria-hidden="true"]

or

svg.a--icon[aria-label="..."][role="img"]
```

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
| `icon` | Specifies the icon. The rendering behavior varies depending on the value provided. |
| `size` | Effective when calling a preset icon. Output as `width` and `height`. |
| `label` | Output as `aria-label`. When specified, `role="img"` is also added; when omitted, `aria-hidden="true"` is output instead. |

## Usage

### Using an external package

Use the standard Lism component props `as` and `exProps`.

This lets you render icons from third-party packages like `react-icons` and `@phosphor-icons/react` through `<Icon>`.

:::warning
Note that when using a React-based icon package in Astro, you need to enable React separately on the Astro side.
:::

<Spacer h="10"/>

  <PreviewTitle>Specifying an external component via `as`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Icon as={SmileyIcon} size="2em" />
    {/* <Icon as={Home} size="2em" /> */}
  <PreviewCode>
```jsx "icon={SmileyIcon}"
import { SmileyIcon } from '@phosphor-icons/react';
import { Icon } from 'lism-css/react';

<Icon as={SmileyIcon} fz="2rem" />
```

To pass props specific to the external component (such as `SmileyIcon`), use `exProps`.

  <PreviewTitle>Specifying props for `SmileyIcon`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Icon as={SmileyIcon} exProps={{ weight: 'fill', size: '3em' }} c="blue" />
  <PreviewCode>
    ```jsx "as=" "exProps="
    <Icon as={SmileyIcon} exProps={{ weight: 'fill', size: '3em' }} c="blue" />
    ```

<Spacer h="10"/>

#### Combining `as` and `exProps` into `icon`

:::point
::title[Point]
In `<Icon>`, you can also pass `as` and `exProps` together in the following format:

```jsx
<Icon icon={{as:Component, exProps1, exProps2, ...}} />
```
:::

  <PreviewTitle>Example of specifying `as` and `exProps` together via `icon`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Icon icon={{ as: SmileyIcon, weight: 'fill', size: '3em' }} c="blue" />
    <PreviewCode slot="tab" label="Combined">
    ```jsx "weight:'fill', size:'3em'" "as:SmileyIcon"
    <Icon icon={{ as: SmileyIcon, weight: 'fill', size: '3em' }} c="blue" />
    ```
  <PreviewCode slot="tab" label="Separate">
    ```jsx "as=" "exProps="
    <Icon as={SmileyIcon} exProps={{ weight: 'fill', size: '3em' }} c="blue" />
    ```

{/* ※ `weight="thin"` is a property available on the `@phosphor-icons` side. */}

{/* <Preview>
  <PreviewTitle>Passing an icon as `children`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Cat className="a--icon" weight="thin" size="3em" />
  <PreviewCode>
    ```jsx
    <Cat className="a--icon" weight="thin" size="3em" />
    ```
</Preview> */}

### Using preset icons

The Lism package (`lism-css`) includes several built-in SVG icons.

You can call a preset icon by specifying its name as a string via `icon='icon-name'`.
([Phosphor Icons](https://phosphoricons.com/) are used.)

<PreviewTitle>Phosphor icon list</PreviewTitle>
<PresetIcons icons={phIcons} />

<PreviewTitle>Logo icon list</PreviewTitle>
<PresetIcons icons={logoIcons} />

  <PreviewTitle>Example of calling a preset icon</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Cluster g="15">
      <Icon icon="lightbulb" size="40px" />
      <Icon icon="warning" fz="2xl" c="blue" />
    </Cluster>
  <PreviewCode>
    ```jsx
    <Cluster g="15">
      <Icon icon="lightbulb" size="40px" />
      <Icon icon="warning" fz="2xl" c="blue" />
    </Cluster>
    ```

### Writing SVG directly

`<Icon>` is rendered as `<svg>` when a `viewBox` prop is specified.
You can place `path` elements and other SVG content directly as children.

  <PreviewTitle>Passing `path` and other elements directly as children</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Icon viewBox="0 0 256 256" label="SmileyIcon icon" fz="4xl" c="blue">
      <path d="M128,24A104,104,0,1,0,232,128,104.11,104.11,0,0,0,128,24Zm0,192a88,88,0,1,1,88-88A88.1,88.1,0,0,1,128,216ZM80,108a12,12,0,1,1,12,12A12,12,0,0,1,80,108Zm96,0a12,12,0,1,1-12-12A12,12,0,0,1,176,108Zm-1.07,48c-10.29,17.79-27.4,28-46.93,28s-36.63-10.2-46.92-28a8,8,0,1,1,13.84-8c7.47,12.91,19.21,20,33.08,20s25.61-7.1,33.07-20a8,8,0,0,1,13.86,8Z"></path>
    </Icon>
    ```jsx
    <Icon viewBox="0 0 256 256" label="SmileyIcon icon" fz="4xl" c="blue">
      <path d="M128,24A104,104,0,1,0,232,128,104.11,104.11,0,0,0,128,24Zm0,192a88,88,0,1,1,88-88A88.1,88.1,0,0,1,128,216ZM80,108a12,12,0,1,1,12,12A12,12,0,0,1,80,108Zm96,0a12,12,0,1,1-12-12A12,12,0,0,1,176,108Zm-1.07,48c-10.29,17.79-27.4,28-46.93,28s-36.63-10.2-46.92-28a8,8,0,1,1,13.84-8c7.47,12.91,19.21,20,33.08,20s25.61-7.1,33.07-20a8,8,0,0,1,13.86,8Z"></path>
    </Icon>
    ```
    ```jsx "--size:"
    <svg
      xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
      viewBox="0 0 256 256"
      width="1em"
      height="1em"
      fill="currentColor"
      focusable="false"
      aria-label="SmileyIcon icon"
      role="img"
      class="a--icon -fz:4xl -c"
      style="--c:var(--blue)"
    >
      <path d="M128,24A104,104,0,1,0,232,128,104.11,104.11,0,0,0,128,24Zm0,192a88,88,0,1,1,88-88A88.1,88.1,0,0,1,128,216ZM80,108a12,12,0,1,1,12,12A12,12,0,0,1,80,108Zm96,0a12,12,0,1,1-12-12A12,12,0,0,1,176,108Zm-1.07,48c-10.29,17.79-27.4,28-46.93,28s-36.63-10.2-46.92-28a8,8,0,1,1,13.84-8c7.47,12.91,19.21,20,33.08,20s25.61-7.1,33.07-20a8,8,0,0,1,13.86,8Z"></path>
    </svg>
    ```

      <span>Img icon.</span>
    </Flex>

# a--spacer.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/primitives/a--spacer.mdx

title: 'Spacer (a--spacer)'
navtitle: 'a--spacer'
description: 'a--spacer is a class for reserving space between elements.'

import { Spacer, Box, Flex } from 'lism-css/astro';

`a--spacer` is a class for reserving space between elements.

## CSS

<SrcCode path="src/scss/primitives/atomic/_spacer.scss" />

## Lism Component

`<Spacer>` is provided as an alias for `<Lism atomic="spacer" aria-hidden="true" />`.

### Import

<ImportPackage component="Spacer" />

### HTML Structure

```pug
div.a--spacer[aria-hidden="true"]
```

### Props

:::info
`<Spacer>` accepts SPACE token values for `w` and `h`.
:::

## Usage

### Basic example

  <PreviewTitle>Usage example of `<Spacer>`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="15" layout="">
    <p>Content...</p>
    <Spacer h="100px" />
    <p>Content...</p>
    ```jsx {2}
    <p>Content...</p>
    <Spacer h="100px" />
    <p>Content...</p>
    ```
    ```html
    <p>Content...</p>
    <div class="a--spacer -h" style="--h:100px" aria-hidden="true"></div>
    <p>Content...</p>
    ```

### Using a SPACE token

  <PreviewTitle>Using a SPACE token</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="15" layout="">
    <p>Box</p>
    <Spacer h="60" />
    <p>Box</p>
    ```jsx {2}
    <p>Box</p>
    <Spacer h="60" />
    <p>Box</p>
    ```
    ```html
    <p>Content...</p>
    <div class="a--spacer -h" style="--h:var(--s60)" aria-hidden="true"></div>
    <p>Content...</p>
    ```

### Horizontal spacer

  <PreviewTitle>Horizontal spacer example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="15" layout="">
    <Flex g="10">
      <Box p="20" bd>Box</Box>
      <Spacer w="40" />
      <Box p="20" bd>Box</Box>
      <Box p="20" bd>Box</Box>
    </Flex>
  <PreviewCode>
    ```jsx "w="
    <Flex g="10">
      <Box p="20" bd>
        Box
      </Box>
      <Spacer w="40" />
      <Box p="20" bd>
        Box
      </Box>
      <Box p="20" bd>
        Box
      </Box>
    </Flex>
    ```

---

# l--autoColumns.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/primitives/l--autoColumns.mdx

title: 'AutoColumns (l--autoColumns)'
navtitle: 'l--autoColumns'
description: 'l--autoColumns is a breakpoint-independent multi-column class where columns automatically wrap before shrinking below a specified minimum width.'

import { AutoColumns, Lism } from 'lism-css/astro';

`l--autoColumns` is a **breakpoint-independent multi-column class** where columns automatically wrap before shrinking below a specified minimum width.

## CSS

<SrcCode path="src/scss/primitives/layout/_autoColumns.scss" />

## Lism Component

### Import

<ImportPackage component="AutoColumns" />

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
| `cols` <PropBadge type="cssvar">`--cols`</PropBadge> | Specifies the minimum width each column should maintain.
| `autoFit` <PropBadge type="cssvar">`--autoMode`</PropBadge> | Switches the repeat mode to `auto-fit` (default is `auto-fill`).

## Usage

### Column size with `--cols`
  <PreviewTitle>Setting the size with `--cols`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <AutoColumns cols="16em" g="20">
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>Item A</Lism>
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>Item B</Lism>
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>Item C</Lism>
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>Item D</Lism>
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>Item E</Lism>
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>Item F</Lism>
    </AutoColumns>
    ```jsx
    <AutoColumns cols="16em" g="20">
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>Item A</Lism>
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>Item B</Lism>
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>Item C</Lism>
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>Item D</Lism>
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>Item E</Lism>
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>Item F</Lism>
    </AutoColumns>
    ```
    ```html "--cols:16em"
    <div class="l--autoColumns -g:20" style="--cols: 16em">
      <div class="-p:20 -bd">Item A</div>
      <div class="-p:20 -bd">Item B</div>
      <div class="-p:20 -bd">Item C</div>
      <div class="-p:20 -bd">Item D</div>
      <div class="-p:20 -bd">Item E</div>
      <div class="-p:20 -bd">Item F</div>
    </div>
    ```

### Using `auto-fit`

In `l--autoColumns`, you can control the first argument of the `repeat()` function in `grid-template-columns` via `--autoMode`. (The default is `auto-fill`.)

Setting `--autoMode: auto-fit` (`autoFit`) changes the behavior when there are only a few items.

  <PreviewTitle>Using `cols=12em` with `auto-fit`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <AutoColumns cols="12em" g="20" fz="s">
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>auto-fill</Lism>
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>auto-fill</Lism>
    </AutoColumns>
    <AutoColumns cols="12em" autoFit g="20" fz="s">
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>auto-fit</Lism>
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>auto-fit</Lism>
    </AutoColumns>
    ```jsx 'autoFit'
    <AutoColumns cols="12em" g="20" fz="s">
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>auto-fill</Lism>
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>auto-fill</Lism>
    </AutoColumns>
    <AutoColumns cols="12em" autoFit g="20" fz="s">
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>auto-fit</Lism>
      <Lism as="div" p="20" bd>auto-fit</Lism>
    </AutoColumns>
    ```
    ```html "--autoMode:auto-fit"
    <div class="l--autoColumns -g:20 -fz:s" style="--cols:12em">
      <div class="-p:20 -bd">auto-fill</div>
      <div class="-p:20 -bd">auto-fill</div>
    </div>
    <div class="l--autoColumns -g:20 -fz:s" style="--cols:12em; --autoMode:auto-fit">
      <div class="-p:20 -bd">auto-fit</div>
      <div class="-p:20 -bd">auto-fit</div>
    </div>
    ```

---

# l--box.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/primitives/l--box.mdx

title: 'Box (l--box)'
navtitle: 'l--box'
description: 'l--box is a simple class that groups content without applying any particular layout behavior.'

import { Box } from 'lism-css/astro';

`l--box` is a simple class that groups content without applying any particular layout behavior.

## Lism Component

### Import

<ImportPackage component="Box" />

## Usage

### Example

  <PreviewTitle>Box example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Box p="30" bgc="base-2" bxsh="10" bdrs="10">
      <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit. Impedit fugit, numquamdicta repellat ipsa autem eos iure ducimus.</p>
    </Box>
    ```jsx
    <Box p="30" bgc="base-2" bxsh="10" bdrs="10">
      <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit. Impedit fugit, numquamdicta repellat ipsa autem eos iure ducimus.</p>
    </Box>
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="l--box -p:30 -bgc:base-2 -bxsh:10 -bdrs:10">
      <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit. Impedit fugit, numquamdicta repellat ipsa autem eos iure ducimus.</p>
    </div>
    ```

# l--center.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/primitives/l--center.mdx

title: 'Center (l--center)'
navtitle: 'l--center'
description: 'l--center is a class for centering elements both horizontally and vertically.'

import { Center, Text } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';

`l--center` is a class for **centering elements both horizontally and vertically**.

## CSS

<SrcCode path="src/scss/primitives/layout/_center.scss" />

## Lism Component

### Import

<ImportPackage component="Center" />

## Usage

### Horizontal centering

When Center has **no height**, it simply aligns its content horizontally centered.

  <PreviewTitle>
    When no height is set
  </PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="15">
    <Center bd p="30">
      <Text fz="l">TEXT</Text>
    </Center>
    ```jsx
    <Center bd p="30">
      <Text fz="l">TEXT</Text>
    </Center>
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="l--center -bd -p:30">
      <p class="-fz:l">TEXT</p>
    </div>
    ```

  <PreviewTitle>
    Long text wraps and stays left-aligned, preserving readability.
  </PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="15">
    <Center bd p="30" g="15">
      <Text fz="l">TEXT</Text>
      <DummyText length="xs" />
      <DummyText />
    </Center>
    ```jsx
    <Center bd p="30" g="15">
      <Text fz="l">TEXT</Text>
      <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.</p>
      <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor Incididunt ut. Labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut.</p>
    </Center>
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="l--center -bd -p:30 -g:15">
      <p class="-fz:l">TEXT</p>
      <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.</p>
      <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor Incididunt ut. Labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut.</p>
    </div>
    ```

### Centering both horizontally and vertically

When Center has a **height or aspect ratio** set, content is also centered vertically.

  <PreviewTitle>
    Centered both horizontally and vertically
  </PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="15">
    <Center g="10" ar="3/2" bd>
      <Text fz="l">TEXT</Text>
      <Text fz="s">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.</Text>
    </Center>
    ```jsx 'ar="3/2"'
    <Center g="10" ar="3/2" bd>
      <Text fz="l">TEXT</Text>
      <Text fz="s">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.</Text>
    </Center>
    ```
    ```html "-ar:3/2"
    <div class="l--center -bd -g:10 -ar:3/2">
      <p class="-fz:l">TEXT</p>
      <p class="-fz:s">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.</p>
    </div>
    ```

---

# l--cluster.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/primitives/l--cluster.mdx

title: 'Cluster (l--cluster)'
navtitle: 'l--cluster'
description: 'l--cluster is a class that arranges multiple elements horizontally and wraps them to the next line when there are too many to fit.'

import { Cluster, Lism } from 'lism-css/astro';

`l--cluster` is a class that **arranges multiple elements horizontally in sequence, wrapping to the next line when there are too many to fit**.

## CSS

<SrcCode path="src/scss/primitives/layout/_cluster.scss" />

## Lism Component

### Import

<ImportPackage component="Cluster" />

## Usage

### Example

  <PreviewTitle>Simple `<Cluster>` example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <Cluster g="15">
      <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">Lorem</Lism>
      <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">ipsum</Lism>
      <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">Dolor</Lism>
      <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">Sit amet</Lism>
      <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">Consectetur</Lism>
      <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">Adipisicing</Lism>
      <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">Elit</Lism>
      <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">Quisquam</Lism>
      <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">Quos</Lism>
    </Cluster>
  ```jsx "Cluster"
  <Cluster g="15">
    <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">
      Lorem
    </Lism>
    <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">
      ipsum
    </Lism>
    <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">
      Dolor
    </Lism>
    <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">
      Sit amet
    </Lism>
    <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">
      Consectetur
    </Lism>
    <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">
      Adipisicing
    </Lism>
    <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">
      Elit
    </Lism>
    <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">
      Quisquam
    </Lism>
    <Lism bd px="10" bdrs="10">
      Quos
    </Lism>
  </Cluster>
  ```
  ```html "l--cluster"
  <div class="l--cluster -g:15">
    <span class="-bd -px:10 -bdrs:10">Lorem</span>
    <span class="-bd -px:10 -bdrs:10">ipsum</span>
    <span class="-bd -px:10 -bdrs:10">Dolor</span>
    <span class="-bd -px:10 -bdrs:10">Sit amet</span>
    <span class="-bd -px:10 -bdrs:10">Consectetur</span>
    <span class="-bd -px:10 -bdrs:10">Adipisicing</span>
    <span class="-bd -px:10 -bdrs:10">Elit</span>
    <span class="-bd -px:10 -bdrs:10">Quisquam</span>
    <span class="-bd -px:10 -bdrs:10">Quos</span>
  </div>
  ```

# l--columns.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/primitives/l--columns.mdx

title: 'Columns (l--columns)'
navtitle: 'l--columns'
description: 'l--columns is a column class that displays content in the specified number of columns at each breakpoint.'
import { Lism, Box, Frame, Media, Columns, Grid, Divider, Heading } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';

`l--columns` is a column class that **displays content in the specified number of columns at each breakpoint**.

## CSS

<SrcCode path="src/scss/primitives/layout/_columns.scss" />

## Lism Component

### Import

<ImportPackage component="Columns" />

### Props

| Prop | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `cols` <PropBadge type="cssvar">`--cols`</PropBadge> | Specifies the number of columns. Breakpoint-based values are also supported. | `2` |

## Usage

### 2-column layout

  <PreviewTitle>
    2-column `<Columns>`
  </PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <Columns cols={2} g="20">
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box</Box>
    </Columns>
    ```jsx "cols={2}"
    <Columns cols={2} g="20">
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box</Box>
    </Columns>
    ```
    ```html "--cols:2"
    <div class="l--columns -g:20" style="--cols: 2">
      <div class="l--box -bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="l--box -bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="l--box -bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="l--box -bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
    </div>
    ```

### 1 → 2 → 3 columns

  <PreviewTitle>1 col → sm: 2 cols → md: 3 cols</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <Columns cols={[1, 2, 3]} g="20">
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box1</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box2</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box3</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box4</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box5</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box6</Box>
    </Columns>
    ```jsx "cols={[1, 2, 3]}"
    <Columns cols={[1, 2, 3]} g="20">
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box1</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box2</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box3</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box4</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box5</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box6</Box>
    </Columns>
    ```
    ```html "--cols:1;--cols_sm:2;--cols_md:3"
    <div class="l--columns -cols_sm -cols_md -g:20" style="--cols: 1; --cols_sm: 2; --cols_md: 3">
      <div class="l--box -bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box1</div>
      <div class="l--box -bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box2</div>
      <div class="l--box -bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box3</div>
      <div class="l--box -bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box4</div>
      <div class="l--box -bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box5</div>
      <div class="l--box -bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box6</div>
    </div>
    ```

### 2 → 4 columns

  <PreviewTitle>2 cols → `@md`: 4 cols</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <Columns cols={[2, null, 4]} g="15">
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box</Box>
      <Box bgc="base-2" p="20">Box</Box>
    </Columns>
    ```jsx "cols={[2, null, 4]}"
    <Columns cols={[2, null, 4]} g="15">
      ...
    </Columns>
    ```
    ```html "--cols:2;--cols_md:4"
    <div class="l--columns -cols_md -g:15" style="--cols: 2; --cols_md: 4">...</div>
    ```

### Using gc (grid-column)
  <PreviewTitle>Alternating 1:2 and 2:1 column spans</PreviewTitle>
    <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <Columns cols="3" g="15">
      <Frame gc="span 1">
        <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-1.jpg" alt="" />
      </Frame>
      <Frame gc="span 2">
        <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-3.jpg" alt="" />
      </Frame>
      <Frame gc="span 2">
        <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-4.jpg" alt="" />
      </Frame>
      <Frame gc="span 1">
        <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-2.jpg" alt="" />
      </Frame>
    </Columns>
    ```jsx 'gc="span 1"' 'gc="span 2"'
    <Columns cols="3" g="15">
      <Frame gc="span 1">
        <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-1.jpg" alt="" />
      </Frame>
      <Frame gc="span 2">
        <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-3.jpg" alt="" />
      </Frame>
      <Frame gc="span 2">
        <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-4.jpg" alt="" />
      </Frame>
      <Frame gc="span 1">
        <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-2.jpg" alt="" />
      </Frame>
    </Columns>
    ```
    ```html "--gc: span 1" "--gc: span 2"
    <div class="l--columns -g:15" style="--cols: 3">
      <div class="l--frame -gc" style="--gc: span 1">
        <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-1.jpg" alt="" />
      </div>
      <div class="l--frame -gc" style="--gc: span 2">
        <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-3.jpg" alt="" />
      </div>
      <div class="l--frame -gc" style="--gc: span 2">
        <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-4.jpg" alt="" />
      </div>
      <div class="l--frame -gc" style="--gc: span 1">
        <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-2.jpg" alt="" />
      </div>
    </div>
    ```

### Using subgrid

A card layout using subgrid inside a 1 → 2 → 3 column grid.

  <PreviewTitle>subgrid</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <Columns cols={[1, 2, 3]} g="20">
      <Grid util="trimAll" g="30" p="20" gtr="subgrid" gr="span 4" bgc="base-2" bdrs="10">
        <Media ar="og" bdrs="10" src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-1.jpg" alt="" inferSize />
        <Heading level="2" hl="s" aslf="center" fz="m">Card Title</Heading>
        <DummyText hl="s" />
        <Lism hl="s" bd-t fz="s" px="10" py="20 10" o="p">Date: 2025-01-01</Lism>
      </Grid>
      <Grid util="trimAll" g="30" p="20" gtr="subgrid" gr="span 4" bgc="base-2" bdrs="10">
        <Media ar="og" bdrs="10" src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-2.jpg" alt="" inferSize />
        <Heading level="2" hl="s" aslf="center" fz="m">Card Title Lorem ipsum</Heading>
        <DummyText hl="s" length="s" />
        <Lism hl="s" bd-t fz="s" px="10" py="20 10" o="p">Date: 2025-01-01</Lism>
      </Grid>
      <Grid util="trimAll" g="30" p="20" gtr="subgrid" gr="span 4" bgc="base-2" bdrs="10">
        <Media ar="og" bdrs="10" src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-3.jpg" alt="" inferSize />
        <Heading level="2" hl="s" aslf="center" fz="m">Card Title, long, long, long, very long long looong.</Heading>
        <DummyText hl="s" />
        <Lism hl="s" bd-t fz="s" px="10" py="20 10" o="p">Date: 2025-01-01</Lism>
      </Grid>
      <Grid util="trimAll" g="30" p="20" gtr="subgrid" gr="span 4" bgc="base-2" bdrs="10">
        <Media ar="og" bdrs="10" src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-4.jpg" alt="" inferSize />
        <Heading level="2" hl="s" aslf="center" fz="m">Card Title</Heading>
        <DummyText hl="s" length="s" />
        <Lism hl="s" bd-t fz="s" px="10" py="20 10" o="p">Date: 2025-01-01</Lism>
      </Grid>
      <Grid util="trimAll" g="20" p="20" gtr="subgrid" gr="span 4" bgc="base-2" bdrs="10">
        <Media ar="og" bdrs="10" src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-5.jpg" alt="" inferSize />
        <Heading level="2" hl="s" aslf="center" fz="m">Card Title</Heading>
        <DummyText hl="s" />
        <Lism hl="s" bd-t fz="s" px="10" py="20 10" o="p">Date: 2025-01-01</Lism>
      </Grid>
    </Columns>
    ```jsx 'gtr="subgrid" gr="span 4"'
    <Columns cols={[1, 2, 3]} g="15">
    ```

# l--flow.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/primitives/l--flow.mdx

title: 'Flow (l--flow)'
navtitle: 'l--flow'
description: 'l--flow is a flow class that manages spacing between child elements using margin.'

import { Flow, Text } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';

`l--flow` is a flow class that manages spacing between child elements using `margin`.  
Use it for text-heavy content layouts such as article bodies.

:::point
Directly under `l--flow`, the spacing between content items is controlled by `--flow` and `margin-block-start`.
:::

| Class name | Spacing amount |
|---|---|
| `l--flow` | `--flow--base` (`--s30`, `--s35` when `lang="ja"`) |
| `.l--flow.-flow:s` | `--flow--s` (`--s20`) |
| `.l--flow.-flow:` | `--flow` |

`--flow--base` / `--flow--s` are design tokens defined on `:root`. In Japanese environments (`lang="ja"`), `--flow--base` is overridden with a slightly larger value to match character density.

Heading tags receive larger spacing than other elements.

## CSS

<SrcCode path="src/scss/primitives/layout/_flow.scss" />

## Lism Component

### Import

<ImportPackage component="Flow" />

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
| `flow` | Sets the value of `--flow`.<br />When `s` is specified, the `-flow:s` class is applied. Any other value is emitted as the `-flow:` class together with the `--flow` variable. |

## Usage

### Basic usage

  <PreviewTitle>`l--flow`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20" layout="">
    <Flow hov="itemGuide">
      <DummyText />
      <h2>Heading 2</h2>
      <DummyText length="s" />
      <DummyText length="l" />
      <h3>Heading 3</h3>
      <ul>
        <li>Lorem ipsum, LIST content...</li>
        <li>Lorem ipsum, LIST content...</li>
        <li>Lorem ipsum, LIST content...</li>
      </ul>
      <DummyText />
    </Flow>
  ```jsx
  <Flow>
    <p>Lorem ipsum content...</p>
    <p>Lorem ipsum content...</p>
    <h2>Heading</h2>
    <p>Lorem ipsum content...</p>
    <p>Lorem ipsum content...</p>
  </Flow>
  ```
  ```html
  <div class="l--flow">
    <p>Lorem ipsum content...</p>
    <p>Lorem ipsum content...</p>
    <h2>Heading</h2>
    <p>Lorem ipsum content...</p>
    <p>Lorem ipsum content...</p>
  </div>
  ```
{/* </Lism> */}

### Using `-flow:s`

  <PreviewTitle>Using `-flow:s`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20" layout="">
    <Flow flow="s" hov="itemGuide">
      <DummyText />
      <h2>Heading 2</h2>
      <DummyText length="s" />
      <DummyText length="l" />
      <h3>Heading 3</h3>
      <ul>
        <li>Lorem ipsum, LIST content...</li>
        <li>Lorem ipsum, LIST content...</li>
        <li>Lorem ipsum, LIST content...</li>
      </ul>
      <DummyText />
    </Flow>
  ```jsx 'flow="s"'
  <Flow flow="s">
    <p>Lorem ipsum content...</p>
    <p>Lorem ipsum content...</p>
    <h2>Heading</h2>
    <p>Lorem ipsum content...</p>
    <p>Lorem ipsum content...</p>
  </Flow>
  ```
  ```html "-flow:s"
  <div class="l--flow -flow:s">
    <p>Lorem ipsum content...</p>
    <p>Lorem ipsum content...</p>
    <h2>Heading</h2>
    <p>Lorem ipsum content...</p>
    <p>Lorem ipsum content...</p>
  </div>
  ```

### Custom value

When a non-token value is passed to `flow`, it is output as the `-flow:` class and `--flow` CSS variable.

  <PreviewTitle>Setting a custom value</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Flow flow="10px" hov="itemGuide">
      <Text>Contents...</Text>
      <h2>Heading</h2>
      <DummyText length="s" />
      <Text>Contents...</Text>
      <Text>Contents...</Text>
    </Flow>
  ```jsx 'flow="10px"'
  <Flow flow="10px">
    <p>Contents...</p>
    <p>Contents...</p>
    <p>Contents...</p>
  </Flow>
  ```
  ```html "--flow:10px"
  <div class="l--flow -flow:" style="--flow: 10px">
    <p>Contents...</p>
    <p>Contents...</p>
    <p>Contents...</p>
  </div>
  ```

Note that `l--flow` falls back to the root-defined `--flow--base` when `--flow` is unset. When nested inside another `l--flow`, it inherits the parent's `--flow` value instead.

### `is--skipFlow`

When used as a direct child of `l--flow`, this class cancels the spacing with the following sibling element.
Use this to place an absolutely positioned element at the start of flow content.

  <PreviewTitle>Example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <div class="l--flow -hov:itemGuide">
      <div class="is--skipFlow">Skip flow...</div>
      <p>Lorem ipsum, Example content...</p>
      <p>Lorem ipsum, Example content...</p>
      <p>Lorem ipsum, Example content...</p>
    </div>
  ```html
  <div class="l--flow">
    <div class="is--skipFlow">skip flow...</div>
    <p>Lorem ipsum, Example content...</p>
    <p>Lorem ipsum, Example content...</p>
    <p>Lorem ipsum, Example content...</p>
  </div>
  ```

## Notes on nesting `l--flow`

When `l--flow` is nested directly inside another `l--flow` and a custom `--flow` is set on the child, that value also affects the child's own `margin-block-start`.
(This issue can be avoided by wrapping the nested `l--flow` in an additional element to avoid being a direct child.)

  <PreviewTitle>When `--flow` is defined on a directly nested `l--flow`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20" layout="">
    <Flow hov="itemGuide">
      <p>Flow contents...</p>
      <p>Flow contents...</p>
      <Flow flow="5px" bgc="orange:10%" hov="itemGuide">
        <p>
          *Nested <code class="-fz:s -bd -p:5 -bdrs:10">`l--flow`(`--flow:5px`)</code>
        </p>
        <p>*Nested flow contents...</p>
      </Flow>
      <p>Flow contents...</p>
      <Flow flow="s" bgc="green:10%" hov="itemGuide">
        <p>
          *Nested <code class="-fz:s -bd -p:5 -bdrs:10">`l--flow`(`--flow:s`)</code>
        </p>
        <p>*Nested flow contents...</p>
      </Flow>
    </Flow>
    ```jsx "\<Flow " '\<Flow flow="5px"'
    <Flow>
      <p>Flow contents...</p>
      <p>Flow contents...</p>
      <Flow flow="5px" bgc="orange:10%">
        <p>
          *Nested <code class="-fz:s -bd -p:5 -bdrs:10">`l--flow`(`--flow:5px`)</code>
        </p>
        <p>*Nested flow contents...</p>
      </Flow>
      <p>Flow contents...</p>
      <Flow flow="s" bgc="green:10%">
        <p>
          *Nested <code class="-fz:s -bd -p:5 -bdrs:10">`l--flow`(`--flow:s`)</code>
        </p>
        <p>*Nested flow contents...</p>
      </Flow>
    </Flow>
    ```

# l--frame.mdx

title: 'Frame (l--frame)'

description: 'l--frame is a class that fits the direct child media element (img, video, iframe) to its own size.'
import { Flex, Layer, Frame, Center } from 'lism-css/astro';

`l--frame` is a class that fits the direct child media element (`img`, `video`, `iframe`) to its own size.

    </Frame>

    <Frame as="figure" ar="16/9" pos="relative">
      <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-1.jpg" alt="" width="960" height="640" />

    ```jsx
        Lorem ipsum text.
      </Flex>
    </Frame>
    ```
    ```html

        Lorem ipsum text.
      </figcaption>
    </figure>
    ```

# l--grid.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/primitives/l--grid.mdx

title: 'Grid (l--grid)'
navtitle: 'l--grid'
description: 'l--grid is a class for arranging content using CSS Grid.'

import { Grid, Lism, Box, Layer, Center, Frame, Media } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';

`l--grid` is a class for **arranging content in a Grid layout**.

## CSS

<SrcCode path="src/scss/primitives/layout/_grid.scss" />

## Lism Component

### Import

<ImportPackage component="Grid" />

## Usage

### Basic usage

  <PreviewTitle>Main content in the center</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="15">
    <Grid gtc="auto 1fr auto" g="15">
      <Center p="20" bgc="base-2">L</Center>
      <Center p="20" bd>Center</Center>
      <Center p="20" bgc="base-2">R</Center>
    </Grid>
    ```jsx
    <Grid gtc="auto 1fr auto" g="15">
      <Center p="20" bgc="base-2">
        L
      </Center>
      <Center p="20" bd>
        Center
      </Center>
      <Center p="20" bgc="base-2">
        R
      </Center>
    </Grid>
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="l--grid -gtc -g:15" style="--gtc: auto 1fr auto">
      <div class="l--center -p:20 -bgc:base-2">L</div>
      <div class="l--center -p:20 -bd">Center</div>
      <div class="l--center -p:20 -bgc:base-2">R</div>
    </div>
    ```

### Switching grid areas at breakpoints

  <PreviewTitle>Switching grid areas at breakpoints</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="15">
    <Grid g="15" gtc={['1fr 1fr', '8em 1fr 8em']} gta={[`'main main' 'left right'`, `'left main right'`]}>
      <Box ga="left" p="15" bgc="base-2">Left</Box>
      <Box ga="main" p="15" bd>Center</Box>
      <Box ga="right" p="15" bgc="base-2">Right</Box>
    </Grid>
    ```jsx
    <Grid g="15" gtc={['1fr 1fr', '8em 1fr 8em']} gta={[`'main main' 'left right'`, `'left main right'`]}>
      <Box ga="left" p="15" bgc="base-2">
        Left
      </Box>
      <Box ga="main" p="15" bd>
        Center
      </Box>
      <Box ga="right" p="15" bgc="base-2">
        Right
      </Box>
    </Grid>
    ```
    ```html
    <div
      class="l--grid -gta -gta_sm -gtc -gtc_sm -g:15"
      style="--gta: 'main main' 'left right'; --gta_sm: 'left main right'; --gtc: 1fr 1fr; --gtc_sm: 8em 1fr 8em"
    >
      <div class="l--box -p:15 -bgc:base-2 -ga" style="--ga: left">Left</div>
      <div class="l--box -p:15 -bd -ga" style="--ga: main">Center</div>
      <div class="l--box -p:15 -bgc:base-2 -ga" style="--ga: right">Right</div>
    </div>
    ```

### Overlapping child elements

This example stacks elements using `grid-area:1/1` (`-ga:1`) without `position:absolute`.

  <PreviewTitle>Overlapping Grid child elements</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="15">
    <Grid ar="16/9">
      <Frame ga="1/1" w="100%" h="100%" pos="relative">
        <Media src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-1.jpg" alt="" inferSize />
        <Layer style={{ backdropFilter: 'blur(10px)' }} bgc="rgb(0 0 0 / 40%)" />
      </Frame>
      <Center ga="1/1" fz="3xl" z="1" c="white">SAMPLE TEXT</Center>
    </Grid>
    ```jsx 'ga="1/1"'
    <Grid ar="16/9">
      <Frame ga="1/1" w="100%" h="100%" pos="relative">
        <Media src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-1.jpg" alt="" inferSize />
        <Layer style={{ backdropFilter: 'blur(10px)' }} bgc="rgb(0 0 0 / 40%)" />
      </Frame>
      <Center ga="1/1" fz="3xl" z="1" c="white">
        SAMPLE TEXT
      </Center>
    </Grid>
    ```
    ```html "-ga:1"
    <div class="l--grid -ar:16/9">
      <div class="l--frame -ga:1/1 -w:100% -h:100% -pos:relative">
        <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-1.jpg" />
        <div class="is--layer -bgc" style="backdrop-filter:blur(10px);--bgc:rgb(0 0 0 / 40%)"></div>
      </div>
      <div class="l--center -ga:1/1 -fz:3xl -z:1 -c" style="--c:var(--white)">
        SAMPLE TEXT
      </div>
    </div>
    ```

### Using subgrid

  <PreviewTitle>Example: building a latest-articles list</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20" resize>
    <Grid gtc={['auto', 'auto 1fr']} bd-b>
      <Grid gtc="subgrid" gc="1/-1" g="20" ai="center" bd-t py="20" px="10">
        <Grid gtc={['auto auto', '1fr 1fr']} g="20" jc="start" ai="center">
          <Lism fz="s">2024.05.31</Lism>
          <Lism d="inline-flex" jc="center" fz="xs" hl="s" bgc="text" c="base" py="5" px="10" bdrs="10">NEWS</Lism>
        </Grid>
        <DummyText util="trim" length="s" as="a" href="####" hov="-o" c="inherit" td="none" hl="s" />
      </Grid>
      <Grid gtc="subgrid" gc="1/-1" g="20" ai="center" bd-t py="20" px="10">
        <Grid gtc={['auto auto', '1fr 1fr']} g="20" jc="start" ai="center">
          <Lism fz="s">2024.05.29</Lism>
          <Lism d="inline-flex" jc="center" fz="xs" hl="s" bgc="text" c="base" py="5" px="10" bdrs="10">TIPS</Lism>
        </Grid>
        <DummyText util="trim" offset="2" as="a" href="####" hov="-o" c="inherit" td="none" hl="s" />
      </Grid>
      <Grid gtc="subgrid" gc="1/-1" g="20" ai="center" bd-t py="20" px="10">
        <Grid gtc={['auto auto', '1fr 1fr']} g="20" jc="start" ai="center">
          <Lism fz="s">2024.05.18</Lism>
          <Lism d="inline-flex" jc="center" fz="xs" hl="s" bgc="text" c="base" py="5" px="10" bdrs="10">COLUMN</Lism>
        </Grid>
        <DummyText util="trim" length="l" offset="6" as="a" href="####" hov="-o" c="inherit" td="none" hl="s" />
      </Grid>
    </Grid>
    ```jsx
    <Grid gtc={['auto', 'auto 1fr']} bd-b>
      <Grid gtc="subgrid" gc="1/-1" g="20" ai="center" bd-t py="20" px="10">
        <Grid gtc={['auto auto', '1fr 1fr']} g="20" jc="start" ai="center">
          <Lism fz="s">2024.05.31</Lism>
          <Lism d="inline-flex" jc="center" fz="xs" hl="s" bgc="text" c="base" py="5" px="10" bdrs="10">
            NEWS
          </Lism>
        </Grid>
        <Text util="trim" as="a" href="####" hov="-o" c="inherit" td="none" hl="s">
          Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor Incididunt ut.
        </Text>
      </Grid>
      <Grid gtc="subgrid" gc="1/-1" g="20" ai="center" bd-t py="20" px="10">
        <Grid gtc={['auto auto', '1fr 1fr']} g="20" jc="start" ai="center">
          <Lism fz="s">2024.05.29</Lism>
          <Lism d="inline-flex" jc="center" fz="xs" hl="s" bgc="text" c="base" py="5" px="10" bdrs="10">
            TIPS
          </Lism>
        </Grid>
        <Text util="trim" as="a" href="####" hov="-o" c="inherit" td="none" hl="s">
          Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor Incididunt ut. Labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut.
        </Text>
      </Grid>
      <Grid gtc="subgrid" gc="1/-1" g="20" ai="center" bd-t py="20" px="10">
        <Grid gtc={['auto auto', '1fr 1fr']} g="20" jc="start" ai="center">
          <Lism fz="s">2024.05.18</Lism>
          <Lism d="inline-flex" jc="center" fz="xs" hl="s" bgc="text" c="base" py="5" px="10" bdrs="10">
            COLUMN
          </Lism>
        </Grid>
        <Text util="trim" as="a" href="####" hov="-o" c="inherit" td="none" hl="s">
          Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.
        </Text>
      </Grid>
    </Grid>
    ```

# l--stack.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/primitives/l--stack.mdx

title: 'Stack (l--stack)'
navtitle: 'l--stack'
description: 'l--stack is a class that arranges multiple elements vertically using a Flex layout.'
import { Stack } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';

`l--stack` is a class that **arranges multiple elements vertically using a Flex layout**.

## CSS

<SrcCode path="src/scss/primitives/layout/_stack.scss" />

## Lism Component

### Import

<ImportPackage component="Stack" />

## Usage

### Basic usage

  <PreviewTitle>Simple `<Stack>` example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="30">
    <Stack g="20" className="has--itemGuide">
      <p>Content</p>
      <p>Content</p>
      <p>Content</p>
    </Stack>
  ```jsx
  <Stack g="20">
    <p>Content</p>
    <p>Content</p>
    <p>Content</p>
  </Stack>
  ```
  ```html
  <div class="l--stack -g:20">
    <p>Content</p>
    <p>Content</p>
    <p>Content</p>
  </div>
  ```

### Center-aligned layout

The combination of `<Stack ai="center">` (`.l--stack.-ai:center`) enables what Every Layout calls **"intrinsic centering"** — content is centered only when it is short enough.

  <PreviewTitle>Intrinsic centering</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize>
    <Stack ai="center" g="20" p="30" className="has--itemGuide">
      <h3 role="presentation">Heading</h3>
      <DummyText length="s" />
      <DummyText length="l" />
    </Stack>
  ```jsx 'ai="center"'
  <Stack ai="center" g="20" p="30">
    <h3>Heading</h3>
    <p>...</p>
    <p>...</p>
  </Stack>
  ```
  ```html "-ai:center"
  <div class="l--stack -ai:center -p:30 -g:20">
    <h3>Heading</h3>
    <p>...</p>
    <p>...</p>
  </div>
  ```

# l--switchColumns.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/primitives/l--switchColumns.mdx

title: 'SwitchColumns (l--switchColumns)'
navtitle: 'l--switchColumns'
description: 'l--switchColumns is a class that switches between multi-column and single-column without using container queries or media queries.'

import { SwitchColumns, Box } from 'lism-css/astro';

`l--switchColumns` is a class that **switches between multi-column and single-column without using container queries or media queries**.

## CSS

<SrcCode path="src/scss/primitives/layout/_switchColumns.scss" />

## Lism Component

### Import

<ImportPackage component="SwitchColumns" />

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
| `breakSize` <PropBadge type="cssvar">`--breakSize`</PropBadge> | Minimum parent width required to keep the horizontal layout. Accepts [sz tokens](/en/docs/tokens/#size). |

## Usage

### Using with the default width

  <PreviewTitle>Using with the default width</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="15">
    <SwitchColumns g="20">
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
    </SwitchColumns>
    ```jsx
    <SwitchColumns g="20">
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
    </SwitchColumns>
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="l--switchColumns -g:20">
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
    </div>
    ```

### Custom breakSize

  <PreviewTitle>Using with a specified `breakSize`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="15">
    <SwitchColumns breakSize="s" g="20">
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
    </SwitchColumns>
    ```jsx
    <SwitchColumns breakSize="s" g="20">
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
    </SwitchColumns>
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="l--switchColumns -g:20" style="--breakSize: var(--sz--s)">
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
    </div>
    ```

### Adjusting proportions with flex-grow

  <PreviewTitle>Adjusting proportions by specifying `flex-grow` on child elements</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="15">
    <SwitchColumns breakSize="s" g="20">
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20" style={{ flexGrow: 2 }}>Box</div>
    </SwitchColumns>
    ```jsx
    <SwitchColumns breakSize="s" g="20">
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20" style={{ flexGrow: 2 }}>
        Box
      </div>
    </SwitchColumns>
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="l--switchColumns -g:20" style="--breakSize: var(--sz--s)">
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20">Box</div>
      <div class="-bgc:base-2 -p:20" style="flex-grow: 2">Box</div>
    </div>
    ```

# l--tileGrid.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/primitives/l--tileGrid.mdx

title: 'TileGrid (l--tileGrid)'
navtitle: 'l--tileGrid'
description: 'l--tileGrid is a class for creating uniform tile-style grid layouts by specifying cols and rows.'

import { TileGrid, Box, Center } from 'lism-css/astro';

`l--tileGrid` is a class for creating **uniform tile-style grid layouts** by specifying `cols` (number of columns) and `rows` (number of rows).

Internally, it uses `grid-template: repeat(rows, 1fr) / repeat(cols, 1fr)`.

## CSS

<SrcCode path="src/scss/primitives/layout/_tileGrid.scss" />

## Lism Component

### Import

<ImportPackage component="TileGrid" />

### Props

| Prop | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `cols` <PropBadge type="cssvar">`--cols`</PropBadge> | Specifies the number of columns. Breakpoint-specific values are supported. | `1` |
| `rows` <PropBadge type="cssvar">`--rows`</PropBadge> | Specifies the number of rows. Breakpoint-specific values are supported. | `1` |

## Usage

### Basic usage

  <PreviewTitle>3-column x 3-row tile grid</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="15">
    <TileGrid cols="3" rows="3" g="5" min-h="50svh">
      <Box p="20" bgc="base-2">item1</Box>
      <Box p="20" bgc="base-2">item2</Box>
      <Box p="20" bgc="base-2">item3</Box>
      <Box p="20" bgc="base-2">item4</Box>
      <Box p="20" bgc="base-2" gc="span 2">item5</Box>
      <Center gc="3" gr="1 / -1" p="20" bgc="blue">item6</Center>
    </TileGrid>
    ```jsx " gc=" " gr="
    <TileGrid cols="3" rows="3" g="5" min-h="50svh">
      <Box p="20" bgc="base-2">
        item1
      </Box>
      <Box p="20" bgc="base-2">
        item2
      </Box>
      <Box p="20" bgc="base-2">
        item3
      </Box>
      <Box p="20" bgc="base-2">
        item4
      </Box>
      <Box p="20" bgc="base-2" gc="span 2">
        item5
      </Box>
      <Center gc="3" gr="1 / -1" p="20" bgc="blue">
        item6
      </Center>
    </TileGrid>
    ```
    ```html "--cols:3;--rows:3"
    <div class="l--tileGrid -g:5" style="--cols: 3; --rows: 3; min-height: 50svh">
      <div class="l--box -bgc:base-2 -p:20">item1</div>
      <div class="l--box -bgc:base-2 -p:20">item2</div>
      <div class="l--box -bgc:base-2 -p:20">item3</div>
      <div class="l--box -bgc:base-2 -p:20">item4</div>
      <div class="l--box -bgc:base-2 -p:20 -gc:span 2">item5</div>
      <div class="l--center -p:20 -bgc:blue" style="grid-column: 3; grid-row: 1 / -1">item6</div>
    </div>
    ```

### Breakpoint-specific values

Both `cols` and `rows` support breakpoint-specific values.

  <PreviewTitle>Example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="15">
    <TileGrid cols={['2', '3']} rows="4" min-h="50svh" gaf="row dense">
      <Box gc={['1 / -1', 'span 2']} gr={['span 2', '1 / -1']} p="20" bgc="base-2">A</Box>
      <Box p="20" bgc="green:20%">B</Box>
      <Box p="20" bgc="blue:20%">C</Box>
      <Box p="20" bgc="red:20%">D</Box>
      <Box p="20" bgc="purple:20%">E</Box>
    </TileGrid>
  <PreviewCode>
    ```jsx "cols={['2', '3']}" 'rows="4"'
    <TileGrid cols={['2', '3']} rows="4" min-h="50svh" gaf="row dense">
      <Box gc={['1 / -1', 'span 2']} gr={['span 2', '1 / -1']} p="20" bgc="base-2">
        A
      </Box>
      <Box p="20" bgc="green:20%">
        B
      </Box>
      <Box p="20" bgc="blue:20%">
        C
      </Box>
      <Box p="20" bgc="red:20%">
        D
      </Box>
      <Box p="20" bgc="purple:20%">
        E
      </Box>
    </TileGrid>
    ```

{/* ## Related

- [`<Columns>`](/en/docs/primitives/l--columns): Column layout with equal widths (1D)
- [`<AutoColumns>`](/en/docs/primitives/l--autoColumns/): Fluid column count with auto-fill / auto-fit
- [`<Grid>`](/en/docs/primitives/l--grid): General-purpose CSS Grid layout */}

# l--withSide.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/primitives/l--withSide.mdx

title: 'WithSide (l--withSide)'
navtitle: 'l--withSide'
description: 'l--withSide is a two-column class that automatically switches between horizontal and vertical arrangements based on the content width you want to preserve.'
import { WithSide, Grid, Box, Frame, Stack } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';

`l--withSide` is a two-column class that, without relying on media queries or container queries, **automatically switches between a horizontal and vertical layout based on the minimum width you want to preserve for the main content**.

- Specify the width of the side content with `--sideW`, and specify the width you want to preserve as much as possible for the main content with `--mainW`.
- While the main content has enough space to maintain `--mainW`, the layout stays horizontal; once it drops below that threshold, it automatically switches to a vertical layout.

Use it for layouts such as "image and content" or "main area and sidebar".

## CSS

<SrcCode path="src/scss/primitives/layout/_withSide.scss" />

One child element must have `is--side`.

```pug
div.l--withSide
  div
  div.is--side
```

## Lism Component

### Import

<ImportPackage component="WithSide" />

### Props

| Prop | Output | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sideW`| <PropBadge type="cssvar">`--sideW`</PropBadge> | Width of the side element |
| `mainW` | <PropBadge type="cssvar">`--mainW`</PropBadge> | Minimum width to maintain for the main element |

## Usage

A child element with `is--side` is required.
The side element uses `--sideW` as its base width. When the main element's width falls below `--mainW`, the layout automatically switches to a single column.

### Usage example

  <PreviewTitle>Usage example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <WithSide sideW="12rem" mainW="20rem" g="20">
      <Box p="15" bd bdc="blue">
        <p>Main Content</p>
        <DummyText />
      </Box>
      <Box isSide p="15" bd bdc="red">
        <p>Side Content</p>
      </Box>
    </WithSide>
    ```jsx "sideW" "isSide"
    <WithSide sideW="12rem" mainW="20rem" g="20">
      <Box p="15" bd bdc="blue">
        <p>Main Content</p>
        <p>
          Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor Incididunt ut. Labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim
          veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut.
        </p>
      </Box>
      <Box isSide p="15" bd bdc="red">
        <p>Side Content</p>
      </Box>
    </WithSide>
    ```
    ```html "is--side" "--sideW"
    <div class="l--withSide -g:20" style="--sideW: 12rem; --mainW: 20rem">
      <div class="l--box -p:15 -bd" style="--bdc: var(--blue)">
        <p>Main Content</p>
        <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit, amet consectetur adipisicing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor. Non facere laudantium ex eos doloribus aut dolore nisi.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="l--box is--side -p:15 -bd" style="--bdc: var(--red)">
        <p>Side Content</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    ```

### Reversed order

Using the `-fxd:row-reverse` class (`flex-direction:row-reverse`) together allows you to reverse only the horizontal order.

:::check
This places the side element on the left when horizontal, and at the bottom when stacked vertically.
:::

  <PreviewTitle>Example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <WithSide fxd="row-reverse" sideW="10rem" mainW="16rem" g="20">
      <Box>
        <DummyText />
      </Box>
      <Box isSide bgc="blue:20%">Side Content</Box>
    </WithSide>
    ```jsx 'fxd="row-reverse"'
    <WithSide fxd="row-reverse" sideW="10rem" mainW="16rem" g="20">
      <Box>
        <p>
          Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor Incididunt ut. Labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim
          veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut.
        </p>
      </Box>
      <Box isSide>Side Content</Box>
    </WithSide>
    ```
    ```html "-fxd:row-reverse"
    <div class="l--withSide -fxd:row-reverse -g:20" style="--sideW: 10rem; --mainW: 16rem">
      <div class="l--box">
        <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, ...</p>
      </div>
      <div class="l--box is--side">Side Content</div>
    </div>
    ```

### Layout with alternating media and text

`l--withSide` also works for layouts that show media and text side by side on wide screens and stacked on narrow screens.

Use this pattern when stacking multiple "media + text" pairs — the media alternates left/right horizontally and stays at the top consistently when stacked vertically.

  <PreviewTitle>Example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <Stack isContainer g="40">
      <WithSide sideW="40%" g="30" ai="center">
        <Frame ar="3/2" isSide max-h="50cqw">
          <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-1.jpg" alt="" width="960" height="640" />
        </Frame>
        <Box px="10"><DummyText /></Box>
      </WithSide>

      <WithSide fxd="row-reverse" sideW="40%" g="30" ai="center">
        <Frame ar="3/2" isSide max-h="50cqw">
          <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-2.jpg" alt="" width="960" height="640" />
        </Frame>
        <Box px="10"><DummyText /></Box>
      </WithSide>
    </Stack>
    ```jsx
    <Stack isContainer g="40">
      <WithSide sideW="40%" g="30" ai="center">
        <Frame ar="3/2" isSide max-h="50cqw">
          <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-1.jpg" alt="" width="960" height="640" />
        </Frame>
        <Box px="10">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.</Box>
      </WithSide>

      <WithSide fxd="row-reverse" sideW="40%" g="30" ai="center">
        <Frame ar="3/2" isSide max-h="50cqw">
          <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-2.jpg" alt="" width="960" height="640" />
        </Frame>
        <Box px="10">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.</Box>
      </WithSide>
    </Stack>
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="l--stack is--container -g:40">
      <div class="l--withSide -g:30 -ai:center" style="--sideW:40%">
        <div class="l--frame is--side -ar:3/2 -max-h" style="--max-h:50cqw">
          <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-1.jpg" alt="" width="960" height="640" />
        </div>
        <div class="l--box -px:10">
          <p>
            Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="l--withSide -fxd:row-reverse -g:30 -ai:center" style="--sideW:40%">
        <div class="l--frame is--side -ar:3/2 -max-h" style="--max-h:50cqw">
          <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-2.jpg" alt="" width="960" height="640" />
        </div>
        <div class="l--box -px:10">
          <p>
            Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    ```

## Building a similar layout with `Grid`

`WithSide` (`l--withSide`) is not dependent on breakpoints, but you can also build a similar layout using [`Grid`](/en/docs/primitives/l--grid) where the switch point is controlled by a breakpoint.

  <PreviewTitle>Building a WithSide-like layout using `Grid`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <Grid gta={[`'.' 'side'`, `'. side'`]} gtc={[null, '1fr 10rem']} g="20">
      <Box>
        <DummyText />
      </Box>
      <Box ga="side" bgc="blue:20%">Side Content</Box>
    </Grid>
    ```jsx "gta=" "gtc="
    <Grid gta={[`'.' 'side'`, `'. side'`]} gtc={[null, '1fr 10rem']} g="20">
      <Box>
        <p>
          Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor Incididunt ut. Labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim
          veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut.
        </p>
      </Box>
      <Box ga="side">Side Content</Box>
    </Grid>
    ```
    ```html "-gta -gta_sm -gtc_sm" "'. side' / 1fr 10rem" "-ga" "--ga:side"
    <div class="l--grid -gta -gta_sm -gtc_sm -g:20" style="--gta: '.' 'side'; --gta_sm: '. side'; --gtc_sm: 1fr 10rem">
      <div class="l--box">
        <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit, amet consectetur adipisicing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor. Non facere laudantium ex eos doloribus aut dolore nisi.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="l--box -ga" style="--ga: side">Side Content</div>
    </div>
    ```

  <PreviewTitle>Example: `side` on the left, switching at `@md`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <Grid gta={[`'.' 'side'`, null, `'side .'`]} gtc={[null, null, '10rem 1fr']} g="20">
      <Box>
        <DummyText />
      </Box>
      <Box ga="side" bgc="blue:20%">Side Content</Box>
    </Grid>
    ```jsx
    <Grid gta={[`'.' 'side'`, null, `'side .'`]} gtc={[null, null, '10rem 1fr']} g="20">
      <Box>
        <p>
          Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor Incididunt ut. Labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim
          veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut.
        </p>
      </Box>
      <Box ga="side">Side Content</Box>
    </Grid>
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="l--grid -gta -gta_md -gtc_md -g:20" style="--gta: '.' 'side'; --gta_md: 'side .'; --gtc_md: 10rem 1fr">
      <div class="l--box">
        <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, ...</p>
      </div>
      <div class="l--box -ga" style="--ga: side">Side Content</div>
    </div>
    ```

---

# property-class.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/property-class.mdx

title: 'Property Class'
description: 'A complete list of Property Classes that map to CSS properties, with usage examples.'
import { Lism, Flow, Container, Frame, Layer, Media, Box, Flex, Grid, Center, Columns, Spacer, Group, Text } from "lism-css/astro";
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';

export const PropTable = ({data={}, ...props}) => {
  const dataKyes = Object.keys(data);
  return (
    <Lism as="table" {...props}>
      {/* <thead className="-ta:left">
        <tr>
          <th>Class</th>
          <th>Value</th>
        </tr>
      </thead> */}
      <tbody>
      {dataKyes.map((_propName) => {
        const utils = data[_propName];
        const utilsKeys = Object.keys(utils);
        return (
          <>
            {utilsKeys.map((utilKey) => {
              return (
                <tr>
                  <td><code>{`-${_propName}:${utilKey}`}</code></td>
                  <td><code>{`${utils[utilKey]}`}</code></td>
                </tr>
              );
            })}
          </>
        )
      })}
      </tbody>
    </Lism>
  );

}

Lism provides utility classes for the most common CSS properties, letting you apply frequently used values and tokens with a single class.
For the most critical properties, responsive breakpoint variants are available too.

These are called **Property Classes** and are defined in the format `-{prop}(:{value})` and `-{prop}_{bp}`.

<PreviewTitle>Examples</PreviewTitle>

```css
.-fz\:l { font-size: var(--fz--l) }
.-fz\:xl { font-size: var(--fz--xl) }
.-ta\:center { text-align: center }
.-d\:none { display: none }
.-p\:20 { --p: var(--s20) }

.-d{display:var(--d)}
.-p,[class*="-p:"]{padding:var(--p)}
@container (min-width: 480px) {
  .-d_sm{display:var(--d_sm)}
  .-p_sm{padding:var(--p);--p:var(--p_sm)!important}
}
@container (min-width: 800px) {
  .-d_md{display:var(--d_md)}
  .-p_md{padding:var(--p);--p:var(--p_md)!important}
}
```

This page lists all available Property Classes.

:::info
You can change which classes are output by [customizing via SCSS](/en/docs/customize/scss/).
:::

{/* ## Full Property Class list
...*/}

## Reading the Tables

Each table covers one group of properties.

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
|**Shorthand**| The abbreviated form of the CSS property. This is the `{prop}` string in the `-{prop}:{val}` class format, and also the prop name used with Lism components.|
|**Property**| The corresponding CSS property |
|**To Class**| Values that are output as Property Utility classes |
|**BP**| Breakpoint support classes (`-{prop}_{bp}`). `✔` covers `sm`, `md`, and `lg`, and `-` means unsupported. |

## Typography

|Shorthand|Property|To Class|BP|
|---|---|---|---|
|`f`|`font`|`inherit`|-|
|`fz`|`font-size`|[`FZ`](/en/docs/tokens/typography/#fz-font-size)|✔|
|`ff`|`font-family`|[`FF`](/en/docs/tokens/typography/#ff-font-family)|-|
|`fw`|`font-weight`|[`FW`](/en/docs/tokens/typography/#fw--font-weight)|-|
|`fs`|`font-style`|`italic`|-|
|`hl`|`line-height` (half-leading)|[`LH`](/en/docs/tokens/half-leading/), <br/>`0`|✔|
|`lh`|`line-height` (compat)|[`LH`](/en/docs/tokens/half-leading/), <br/>`1`|-|
|`lts`|`letter-spacing`|[`LTS`](/en/docs/tokens/typography/#lts-letter-spacing)|-|
|`ta`|`text-align`|`center`<br/>`left`<br/>`right`|-|
|`td`|`text-decoration`|`none`|-|
|`tt`|`text-transform`|`upper`<br/>`lower`|-|

  <PreviewTitle>Examples</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="30">
    <p class="-fz:xl -fw:bold -lts:l -ta:center -tt:upper">Example text</p>
  ```html
  <p class="-fz:xl -fw:bold -lts:l -ta:center -tt:upper">Example text</p>
  ```
  ```jsx
  <Text fz="xl" fw="bold" lts="l" ta="center" tt="upper">
    Example text
  </Text>
  ```

  ```html "-jc:between"
  </div>
  ```
  ```jsx 'jc="between"'
  <Flex jc="between">
    <Lism bd p="10" bgc="base-2">Item 1</Lism>
    <Lism bd p="10" bgc="base-2">Item 2</Lism>
  </Flex>
  ```

{/* |`place-items`|`pi`|-|-|
|`place-content`|`pc`|-|-|
|`place-self`|`pslf`|-|-| */}

## Styling

### Shadow & Radius

|Shorthand|Prop|To Class|BP|
|---|---|---|---|
|`bxsh`|`box-shadow`|[`SHADOW`](/en/docs/tokens/#shadow)|✔|
|`bdrs`|`border-radius`|[`RADIUS`](/en/docs/tokens/#radius)|✔|

  <PreviewTitle>Examples</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="30">
    <Lism bxsh="20" bdrs="20" p="20" bd>
      <Fragment>Box</Fragment>
    </Lism>
  ```html '-bxsh:20' '-bdrs:20'
  <div class="-bxsh:20 -bdrs:20 -p:20 -bd">Box</div>
  ```
  ```jsx 'bxsh="20"' 'bdrs="20"'
  <Lism bxsh="20" bdrs="20" p="20" bd>Box</Lism>
  ```

### Border

|Shorthand|Prop|To Class|BP|
|---|---|---|---|
|`bd`|`border`|`none`|-|
|`bdc`|`--bdc`|`brand`,`accent`<br />`divider`,<br />`inherit`,<br />`transparent`|-|
|`bds`|`--bds`|`dashed`,`dotted`,`double`|-|
|`bdw`|`--bdw`|-|✔|
|`bd-t`|`border-top`|-|-|
|`bd-r`|`border-right`|-|-|
|`bd-b`|`border-bottom`|-|-|
|`bd-l`|`border-left`|-|-|
|`bd-x`|`border-inline`|-|-|
|`bd-y`|`border-block`|-|-|
|`bd-s`|`border-inline-start`|-|-|
|`bd-e`|`border-inline-end`|-|-|
|`bd-bs`|`border-block-start`|-|-|
|`bd-be`|`border-block-end`|-|-|

  <PreviewTitle>Examples</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="30">
    <Lism bd bdc="current" bds="dashed" bdw="2px" p="20">
      <Text>Box</Text>
    </Lism>
  ```html '-bd -bdc:current -bds:dashed' '--bdw:2px'
  <div class="-bd -bdc:current -bds:dashed -p:20" style="--bdw:2px"><p>Box</p></div>
  ```
  ```jsx 'bd bdc="current" bds="dashed" bdw="2px"'
  <Lism bd bdc="current" bds="dashed" bdw="2px" p="20">Box</Lism>
  ```

<Spacer h="10" />
:::info
The border specification has some unique behavior. See the [border page](/en/docs/property-class/bd/) for details.
:::

<DocsLink path="/docs/property-class/bd/" />

  ```html "-wm_sm" "--wm_sm:"
    <p>
      Labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut. Aliquip ex ea commodo consequat. Duis aute irure dolor in reprehenderit in voluptate velit esse cillum dolore eu fugiat nulla pariatur. Excepteur sint.
    </p>
  </div>
  ```
  ```jsx 'wm={[null, "vertical-rl"]}'
  <Flow hasGutter py="20" w="100%" h="20em" wm={[null, 'vertical-rl']}>
    <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor Incididunt ut.</p>
    <p>
      Labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut. Aliquip ex ea commodo consequat. Duis aute irure dolor in reprehenderit in voluptate velit esse cillum dolore eu fugiat nulla pariatur. Excepteur sint.
    </p>
  </Flow>
  ```

## hover

In Lism, hover styles use Property Classes prefixed with `-hov:`. These work a little differently from regular Property Classes.

See the [hover page](/en/docs/property-class/hov/) for details.

# bd.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/property-class/bd.mdx

title: '-bd'
description: 'How to use the -bd property classes and related CSS variables for border styling.'
import { Box, Flex, Stack, Divider, Spacer } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';

Border-related properties in Lism follow a slightly different convention.

- Use the `-bd` class to show a border on all sides.
- To show a border on a single side, use the `-bd-{side}` class. In addition to the block / inline directions, the top / right / bottom / left directions are also supported.
- Three variables control the fine-grained styling of these borders: `--bdc`, `--bdw`, and `--bds`.
- To change the border direction at a breakpoint, adjust `--bdw`.

<PreviewTitle>css</PreviewTitle>
```scss
:where(.-bd, [class*=' -bd-'], [class^='-bd-']) {
  --bds: solid;
  --bdw: 1px;
  --bdc: var(--divider);
  border-width: var(--bdw);
  border-color: var(--bdc);
}
.-bd {
  border-style: var(--bds);
}
.-bd-x {
  border-inline-style: var(--bds);
}
.-bd-y {
  border-block-style: var(--bds);
}
.-bd-s {
  border-inline-start-style: var(--bds);
}
.-bd-e {
  border-inline-end-style: var(--bds);
}
.-bd-bs {
  border-block-start-style: var(--bds);
}
.-bd-be {
  border-block-end-style: var(--bds);
}
.-bd-t {
  border-top-style: var(--bds);
}
.-bd-b {
  border-bottom-style: var(--bds);
}
.-bd-l {
  border-left-style: var(--bds);
}
.-bd-r {
  border-right-style: var(--bds);
}
```

Accordingly, components also accept `bd`, `bd-{side}`, `bdc`, `bdw`, and `bds`, where `bdc`, `bdw`, and `bds` are output as CSS variables.

Additionally, `bdw` supports breakpoint specification.

  <PreviewTitle>Usage example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="30">
    <Box bd p="10">
      <DummyText length="s" />
    </Box>
    <Box bd bds="dashed" bdw="4px" bdc="red" p="15">
      <DummyText length="s" />
    </Box>
  <PreviewCode label="JSX" slot="tab">
    ```jsx
    <Box bd p="10">
      <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor Incididunt ut.</p>
    </Box>
    <Box bd bds="dashed" bdw="4px" bdc="red" p="15">
      <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor Incididunt ut.</p>
    </Box>
    ```
  <PreviewCode label="HTML" slot="tab">
    ```html "-bd" "--bdc" "--bdw" "--bds"
    <div class="l--box -bd -p:10">
      <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipisicing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="l--box -bd -bds:dashed -p:15" style="--bdw: 4px; --bdc: var(--red)">
      <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipisicing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor.</p>
    </div>
    ```

## Side Specification

:::info
To apply a border on only one side, use the `-bd-{side}` class.
:::

  <PreviewTitle>Specifying all 4 sides</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="30" flow="50">
    <Box bd-t px="10">
      <Fragment>-t: Top</Fragment>
    </Box>
    <Box bd-r px="10">
      <Fragment>-r: Right</Fragment>
    </Box>
    <Box bd-b px="10">
      <Fragment>-b: Bottom</Fragment>
    </Box>
    <Box bd-l px="10">
      <Fragment>-l: Left</Fragment>
    </Box>
  <PreviewCode label="JSX" slot="tab">
    ```jsx "bd-t" "bd-r" "bd-b" "bd-l"
    <Box bd-t px="10">-t: Top</Box>
    <Box bd-r px="10">-r: Right</Box>
    <Box bd-b px="10">-b: Bottom</Box>
    <Box bd-l px="10">-l: Left</Box>
    ```
  <PreviewCode label="HTML" slot="tab">
    ```html "-bd-t" "-bd-r" "-bd-b" "-bd-l"
    <div class="l--box -bd-t -px:10">-t: Top</div>
    <div class="l--box -bd-r -px:10">-r: Right</div>
    <div class="l--box -bd-b -px:10">-b: Bottom</div>
    <div class="l--box -bd-l -px:10">-l: Left</div>
    ```

  <PreviewTitle>Specifying block and inline directions</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="30" flow="50">
    <Box bd-s bdw="2px" px="10" bgc="base-2">
      <Fragment>inline-start</Fragment>
    </Box>
    <Box bd-e bdw="2px" px="10" bgc="base-2">
      <Fragment>inline-end</Fragment>
    </Box>
    <Box bd-bs bdw="2px" px="10" bgc="base-2">
      <Fragment>block-start</Fragment>
    </Box>
    <Box bd-be bdw="2px" px="10" bgc="base-2">
      <Fragment>block-end</Fragment>
    </Box>
    <Box bd-x bdw="2px" px="10" bgc="base-2">
      <Fragment>inline</Fragment>
    </Box>
    <Box bd-y bdw="2px" px="10" bgc="base-2">
      <Fragment>block</Fragment>
    </Box>
  <PreviewCode label="JSX" slot="tab">
    ```jsx "bd-x" "bd-y" "bd-s" "bd-e" "bd-bs" "bd-be"
    <Box bd-s bdw="2px" px="10" bgc="base-2">inline-start</Box>
    <Box bd-e bdw="2px" px="10" bgc="base-2">inline-end</Box>
    <Box bd-bs bdw="2px" px="10" bgc="base-2">block-start</Box>
    <Box bd-be bdw="2px" px="10" bgc="base-2">block-end</Box>
    <Box bd-x bdw="2px" px="10" bgc="base-2">inline</Box>
    <Box bd-y bdw="2px" px="10" bgc="base-2">block</Box>
    ```
  <PreviewCode label="HTML" slot="tab">
    ```html "-bd-x" "-bd-y" "-bd-s" "-bd-e" "-bd-bs" "-bd-be"
    <div class="l--box -bd-s -px:10 -bgc:base-2" style="--bdw: 2px">inline-start</div>
    <div class="l--box -bd-e -px:10 -bgc:base-2" style="--bdw: 2px">inline-end</div>
    <div class="l--box -bd-bs -px:10 -bgc:base-2" style="--bdw: 2px">block-start</div>
    <div class="l--box -bd-be -px:10 -bgc:base-2" style="--bdw: 2px">block-end</div>
    <div class="l--box -bd-x -px:10 -bgc:base-2" style="--bdw: 2px">inline</div>
    <div class="l--box -bd-y -px:10 -bgc:base-2" style="--bdw: 2px">block</div>
    ```

<Spacer h="10" />

When different styles are needed for each side, you can combine the `-bd` class with `--bdw`, `--bds`, and `--bdc` as follows:

  <PreviewTitle>Per-side specification of `bdw`, `bds`, `bdc`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="30">
    <Box bd bdw="0 0 1px .5em" bds="dashed solid" bdc="var(--purple) var(--blue)" p="15">
      <Fragment>border</Fragment>
    </Box>
  <PreviewCode label="JSX" slot="tab">
    ```jsx
    <Box bd bdw="0 0 1px .5em" bds="dashed solid" bdc="var(--purple) var(--blue)" p="15">
      border
    </Box>
    ```
  <PreviewCode label="HTML" slot="tab">
    ```html
    <div class="l--box -bd -p:15" style="--bdw: 0 0 1px 0.5em; --bds: dashed solid; --bdc: var(--purple) var(--blue)">border</div>
    ```

## Switching `bdw` at breakpoints

`bdw` supports breakpoint specification.

  <PreviewTitle>Example of `bd`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="30" resize>
    <Box bd bdw={['1px', '3px', '6px']} p="15">
      <Fragment>border</Fragment>
    </Box>
  <PreviewCode label="JSX" slot="tab">
    ```jsx
    <Box bd bdw={['1px', '3px', '6px']} p="15">
      border
    </Box>
    ```
  <PreviewCode label="HTML" slot="tab">
    ```html
    <div class="l--box -bd -bdw_sm -bdw_md -p:15" style="--bdw: 1px; --bdw_sm: 3px; --bdw_md: 6px">border</div>
    ```

### Switching the border side

By switching `bdw` at breakpoints, you can also change which side the border appears on.

  <PreviewTitle>Switching the border side</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="30" resize>
    <Flex fxd={['column', 'row']}>
      <Box px="15" py="5">
        <Fragment>Box</Fragment>
      </Box>
      <Box px="15" py="5" bd-s bd-bs bdw={['1px 0', '0 1px']}>
        <Fragment>Box</Fragment>
      </Box>
      <Box px="15" py="5" bd-s bd-bs bdw={['1px 0', '0 1px']}>
        <Fragment>Box</Fragment>
      </Box>
    </Flex>
  <PreviewCode label="JSX" slot="tab">
    ```jsx
    <Flex fxd={['column', 'row']}>
      <Box px="15" py="5">
        Box
      </Box>
      <Box px="15" py="5" bd-s bd-bs bdw={['1px 0', '0 1px']}>
        Box
      </Box>
      <Box px="15" py="5" bd-s bd-bs bdw={['1px 0', '0 1px']}>
        Box
      </Box>
    </Flex>
    ```
  <PreviewCode label="HTML" slot="tab">
    ```html
    <div class="l--flex -fxd:column -fxd_sm" style="--fxd_sm: row">
      <div class="l--box -px:15 -py:5">Box</div>
      <div class="l--box -px:15 -py:5 -bd-s -bd-bs -bdw_sm" style="--bdw: 1px 0; --bdw_sm: 0 1px">Box</div>
      <div class="l--box -px:15 -py:5 -bd-s -bd-bs -bdw_sm" style="--bdw: 1px 0; --bdw_sm: 0 1px">Box</div>
    </div>
    ```

{/*
## Outputting arbitrary `border` values inline

You can also pass a value directly to `bd`.

  <PreviewTitle>Example of `bd`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="30" resize>
    <Box bd="solid 1px #555" p="10">
      border
    </Box>
  <PreviewCode label="JSX" slot="tab">
    ```jsx
    <Box bd="solid 1px #555" p="10">
      border
    </Box>
    ```
  <PreviewCode label="HTML" slot="tab">
    ```html
    <div class="l--box -p:10" style="border: solid 1px #555">border</div>
    ```
</Preview> */}

{/* To specify an arbitrary value for individual border sides (such as `border-left` or `border-top`), use the `borders` prop.

`borders` accepts an object where you can specify `l`, `r`, `t`, `b`, `ie`, `is`, `be`, `bs`.
These are output simply as inline styles.

  <PreviewTitle>bdl,bdb</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="30">
    <Box borders={{ l: 'solid 4px green', b: 'solid 1px blue' }} px="10">
      left,bottom
    </Box>
  <PreviewCode label="JSX" slot="tab">
    ```jsx
    <Box borders={{ l: 'solid 4px green', b: 'solid 1px blue' }} px="10">
      left,bottom
    </Box>
    ```
  <PreviewCode label="HTML" slot="tab">
    ```html
    <div class="l--box" style="border-left: solid 4px green; border-bottom: solid 1px blue">left,bottom</div>
    ```
</Preview> */}
