# Accordion.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/ui/Accordion.mdx

title: 'Accordion'
description: 'Documentation for the Accordion component provided by @lism-css/ui.'

import { Divider, Stack, Center, Flex, Icon } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { Accordion } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/Accordion';
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';

A UI component for creating accordion elements.

It is built with `<div>` / `<button>` elements rather than `<details>` / `<summary>`, and uses JavaScript to control the open/close animation.
The panel uses `hidden="until-found"`, so its content can be discovered by the browser's in-page search even when the accordion is closed, and the panel will automatically expand when a match is found.

  <PreviewTitle>Preview</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Accordion.Root bd>
      <Accordion.Item>
        <Accordion.Heading>
          <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Example 1</Accordion.Button>
        </Accordion.Heading>
        <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
          <DummyText length="l" />
        </Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
      <Accordion.Item bd-t>
        <Accordion.Heading>
          <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Example 2</Accordion.Button>
        </Accordion.Heading>
        <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
          <DummyText length="l" />
        </Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
    </Accordion.Root>
    ```jsx
    <Accordion.Root>
      <Accordion.Item>
        <Accordion.Heading>
          <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Example</Accordion.Button>
        </Accordion.Heading>
        <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
          <DummyText length="l" />
        </Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
      <Accordion.Item bd-t>
        <Accordion.Heading>
          <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Example 2</Accordion.Button>
        </Accordion.Heading>
        <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
          <DummyText length="l" />
        </Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
    </Accordion.Root>
    ```
```html
```

## Usage

Provided as `Accordion` from the `@lism-css/ui` package.

### Import

<ImportPackage component="Accordion" script="accordion.js" packageName="@lism-css/ui" />

The following components are available:

- `<Accordion.Root>`: The root element wrapping multiple accordion items (based on `Stack`)
- `<Accordion.Item>`: An individual accordion element
- `<Accordion.Heading>`: Wrapper for the heading area (defaults to `<div role="heading">`)
- `<Accordion.Button>`: The toggle button (automatically includes `<Accordion.Icon>` at the end)
- `<Accordion.Icon>`: The open/close state indicator icon (rendered via CSS pseudo-elements)
- `<Accordion.Panel>`: The content panel that opens and closes (uses `hidden="until-found"`)

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
| <PropBadge>`<Accordion.Root>`</PropBadge><br/>`allowMultiple` | Allows multiple accordions to be expanded simultaneously. By default, only one can be open at a time. |
| <PropBadge>`<Accordion.Item>`</PropBadge><br/>`isOpen` | Expands the item by default (adds `data-opened`). Use together with `isOpen` on `<Accordion.Button>` / `<Accordion.Panel>`. |
| <PropBadge>`<Accordion.Heading>`</PropBadge><br/>`as` | Specifies the HTML tag for the heading. Defaults to `div` (with `role="heading"` added automatically). If `h2`–`h6` is specified, `role` is not added. |
| <PropBadge>`<Accordion.Button>`</PropBadge><br/>`isOpen` | Sets `aria-expanded` to match the initial expanded state. |
| <PropBadge>`<Accordion.Panel>`</PropBadge><br/>`flow` | Flow layout setting passed to the content area (`__content`) inside the panel. |
| <PropBadge>`<Accordion.Panel>`</PropBadge><br/>`isOpen` | Shows the panel by default (removes `hidden`). |

### Structure

```jsx
<Accordion.Root>
  <Accordion.Item>
    <Accordion.Heading>
      <Accordion.Button>Accordion Label</Accordion.Button>
    </Accordion.Heading>
    <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
      ...Contents...
    </Accordion.Panel>
  </Accordion.Item>
</Accordion.Root>
```

:::note
`<Accordion.Button>` automatically includes `<Accordion.Icon>` at the end.
The icon is rendered using CSS pseudo-elements (`::before` / `::after`), so no SVG specification is needed.
:::

### Source Code

The source code is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/tree/main/packages/lism-ui/src/components/Accordion).

## Examples

### Changing the heading tag

`<Accordion.Heading>` outputs a `<div role="heading">` by default, but you can specify a heading tag like `h3` via the `as` prop to render it as an actual heading element.

  <PreviewTitle>Example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Accordion.Root bd>
      <Accordion.Item>
        <Accordion.Heading as="h3">
          <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Label</Accordion.Button>
        </Accordion.Heading>
        <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
          <DummyText length="l" />
        </Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
      <Accordion.Item bd-t>
        <Accordion.Heading as="h3">
          <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Label</Accordion.Button>
        </Accordion.Heading>
        <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
          <DummyText length="l" />
        </Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
    </Accordion.Root>
    ```jsx 'as="h3"'
    <Accordion.Root bd>
      <Accordion.Item>
        <Accordion.Heading as="h3">
          <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Label</Accordion.Button>
        </Accordion.Heading>
        <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
          <DummyText length="l" />
        </Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
      <Accordion.Item bd-t>
        <Accordion.Heading as="h3">
          <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Label</Accordion.Button>
        </Accordion.Heading>
        <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
          <DummyText length="l" />
        </Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
    </Accordion.Root>
    ```
  ```html "h3"
  <div class="c--accordion l--stack">
    <div class="c--accordion_item">
      <h3 class="c--accordion_heading set--plain">
        <button class="c--accordion_button l--flex set--plain -g:10 -w:100% -ai:center -jc:between" aria-controls="{id}" aria-expanded="false">
          Accordion Label
          <span class="c--accordion_icon a--icon -pi:center -fxsh:0" aria-hidden="true"></span>
        </button>
      </h3>
      ...
    </div>
  </div>
  ```

### Changing the animation duration

The speed of the open/close animation is controlled by the `--duration` variable, which defaults to `0.25s`.
You can change it by setting the CSS variable on `<Accordion.Root>` (for all items) or on an individual `<Accordion.Item>`.

  <PreviewTitle>Preview</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Accordion.Root bd style={{ '--duration': '.15s' }}>
      <Accordion.Item>
        <Accordion.Heading>
          <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Example 1</Accordion.Button>
        </Accordion.Heading>
        <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
          <DummyText length="l" />
        </Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
      <Accordion.Item bd-t>
        <Accordion.Heading>
          <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Example 2</Accordion.Button>
        </Accordion.Heading>
        <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
          <DummyText length="l" />
        </Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
    </Accordion.Root>
```jsx "--duration"
<Accordion.Root style={{ '--duration': '.15s' }}>
  <Accordion.Item>
    <Accordion.Heading>
      <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Example 1</Accordion.Button>
    </Accordion.Heading>
    <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
      ...
    </Accordion.Panel>
  </Accordion.Item>
  ...
</Accordion.Root>
```
```html "--duration"
<div class="c--accordion l--stack" style="--duration: 0.15s">
  <div class="c--accordion_item">...</div>
  <div class="c--accordion_item">...</div>
</div>
```

### Opening the first item by default

To have an item expanded from the start, specify `isOpen` on each of `<Accordion.Item>`, `<Accordion.Button>`, and `<Accordion.Panel>`.

:::note
Because `isOpen` plays a different role on each component, specify it on all three.
On `<Accordion.Item>` it adds `data-opened` to set the panel height and icon to the open state, on `<Accordion.Button>` it controls `aria-expanded`, and on `<Accordion.Panel>` it toggles `hidden`.
:::

  <PreviewTitle>Preview</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Accordion.Root bd>
      <Accordion.Item isOpen>
        <Accordion.Heading>
          <Accordion.Button p="20" isOpen>Accordion Label 1</Accordion.Button>
        </Accordion.Heading>
        <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5" isOpen>
          <DummyText length="l" />
        </Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
      <Accordion.Item bd-t>
        <Accordion.Heading>
          <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Label 2</Accordion.Button>
        </Accordion.Heading>
        <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
          <DummyText length="l" />
        </Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
    </Accordion.Root>
```jsx "isOpen"
<Accordion.Root bd>
  <Accordion.Item isOpen>
    <Accordion.Heading>
      <Accordion.Button p="20" isOpen>Accordion Label 1</Accordion.Button>
    </Accordion.Heading>
    <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5" isOpen>
      ...
    </Accordion.Panel>
  </Accordion.Item>
  <Accordion.Item bd-t>
    <Accordion.Heading>
      <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Label 2</Accordion.Button>
    </Accordion.Heading>
    <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
      ...
    </Accordion.Panel>
  </Accordion.Item>
</Accordion.Root>
```
```html "data-opened"
<div class="c--accordion l--stack">
  <div class="c--accordion_item" data-opened>
    <!-- button: aria-expanded="true" / panel: no hidden -->
    ...
  </div>
  <div class="c--accordion_item">...</div>
</div>
```

### Allowing multiple panels to be open

:::note
By default, only one accordion within the same `<Accordion.Root>` can be expanded at a time.
Specifying `allowMultiple` allows multiple panels to be open simultaneously.
:::

  <PreviewTitle>Preview</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Accordion.Root allowMultiple bd>
      <Accordion.Item>
        <Accordion.Heading>
          <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Label 1</Accordion.Button>
        </Accordion.Heading>
        <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
          <DummyText length="l" />
        </Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
      <Accordion.Item bd-t>
        <Accordion.Heading>
          <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Label 2</Accordion.Button>
        </Accordion.Heading>
        <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
          <DummyText length="xl" />
        </Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
      <Accordion.Item bd-t>
        <Accordion.Heading>
          <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Label 3</Accordion.Button>
        </Accordion.Heading>
        <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
          <DummyText length="l" />
        </Accordion.Panel>
      </Accordion.Item>
    </Accordion.Root>
```jsx "allowMultiple"
<Accordion.Root allowMultiple bd>
  <Accordion.Item>
    <Accordion.Heading>
      <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Label 1</Accordion.Button>
    </Accordion.Heading>
    <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
      ...
    </Accordion.Panel>
  </Accordion.Item>
  <Accordion.Item bd-t>
    <Accordion.Heading>
      <Accordion.Button p="20">Accordion Label 2</Accordion.Button>
    </Accordion.Heading>
    <Accordion.Panel p="20" pt="5">
      ...
    </Accordion.Panel>
  </Accordion.Item>
  ...
</Accordion.Root>
```
```html "data-allow-multiple"
<div class="c--accordion l--stack" data-allow-multiple>
  <div class="c--accordion_item">...</div>
  <div class="c--accordion_item">...</div>
  <div class="c--accordion_item">...</div>
</div>
```

{/* Internally uses `<WithSide>`. The content side automatically stacks vertically when its width falls below a certain threshold. */}

## Usage

Import `Alert` from the `@lism-css/ui` package.

### Import
<ImportPackage component="Alert" packageName="@lism-css/ui" />

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
|`type`| Specifies a keyword that sets a combination of `keycolor` and `icon`. Default: `"alert"` |
|`icon`| Specifies the icon to pass to the [`Icon`](/docs/primitives/a--icon/) component. |
|`keycolor`| Specifies the key color. |
|`flow`| Passed to the `flow` prop of the `Flow` element that wraps the content. |
|`layout`| Switches the layout primitive. Default: `"flex"` |

### Source Code

The source code is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/tree/main/packages/lism-ui/src/components/Alert).

# Avatar.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/ui/Avatar.mdx

title: 'Avatar'
description: 'Documentation for the Avatar component provided by @lism-css/ui.'
import { Flex, Center, Frame } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { Avatar } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/Avatar';

A component for displaying avatar images.

  <PreviewTitle>Preview</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20" bg=":stripe">
    <Avatar size="4rem" src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-01.jpg" alt="Avatar of xxxx" />
  <PreviewCode slot="tab" label="React / Astro">
    ```jsx
    <Avatar size="4rem" src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-01.jpg" alt="Avatar of xxxx" />
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="c--avatar l--frame -ar:1/1 -w -bdrs:99" style="--w: 4rem">
      <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-01.jpg" alt="Avatar of xxxx" width="100%" height="100%" decoding="async" />
    </div>
    ```

## Usage

Provided as `Avatar` (`c--avatar`) from the `@lism-css/ui` package.

### Import

<ImportPackage component="Avatar" packageName="@lism-css/ui" />

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
|`size`| Specifies the size of the avatar. |
|`src`| Path to the avatar image. |
|`alt`| Alt text for the image. |

### Source Code

The source code is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/tree/main/packages/lism-ui/src/components/Avatar).

## Examples

  <PreviewTitle>`Avatar` examples</PreviewTitle>

      <Avatar size="4rem" src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-01.jpg" alt="Avatar of xxxx" />
      <Avatar size="5rem" src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-02.jpg" alt="Avatar of xxxx" bd bdw="2px" bdc="base" bxsh="20" />
    </Flex>
    ```jsx
    <Avatar size="4rem" src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-01.jpg" alt="Avatar of xxxx"/>
    <Avatar size="5rem" src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-02.jpg" alt="Avatar of xxxx" bd bdw="2px" bdc="base" bxsh="20"/>
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="c--avatar l--frame -ar:1/1 -w -bdrs:99" style="--w: 4rem">
      <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-01.jpg" alt="Avatar of xxxx" width="100%" height="100%" decoding="async" />
    </div>
    <div class="c--avatar l--frame -ar:1/1 -w -bdrs:99 -bd -bxsh:20" style="--w: 5rem; --bdw: 2px; --bdc: var(--base)">
      <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-02.jpg" alt="Avatar of xxxx" width="100%" height="100%" decoding="async" />
    </div>
    ```

# Badge.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/ui/Badge.mdx

title: 'Badge'
description: 'Documentation for the Badge component provided by @lism-css/ui.'
import { Lism, Cluster, Flex, Icon, Spacer } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { Badge } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/Badge';

A component for displaying badges.

  <PreviewTitle>Preview</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20" bg=":stripe">
    <Cluster g="15">
      <Badge>Badge</Badge>
      <Badge variant="outline">Badge</Badge>
      <Badge util="cbox" keycolor="blue" bdrs="99">
        <Fragment>Badge</Fragment>
      </Badge>
    </Cluster>
  <PreviewCode slot="tab" label="React / Astro">
    ```jsx
    <Cluster g="15">
      <Badge>Badge</Badge>
      <Badge variant="outline">Badge</Badge>
      <Badge util="cbox" keycolor="blue" bdrs="99">
        Badge
      </Badge>
    </Cluster>
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="l--cluster -g:15">
      <span class="c--badge -d:inline-flex -fz:xs -hl:xs -py:5 -px:10 -bdrs:10">Badge</span>
      <span class="c--badge c--badge--outline -d:inline-flex -fz:xs -hl:xs -py:5 -px:10 -bdrs:10">Badge</span>
      <span class="c--badge u--cbox -d:inline-flex -fz:xs -hl:xs -py:5 -px:10 -bdrs:99" style="--keycolor:var(--blue)">
        Badge
      </span>
    </div>
    ```

## Usage

Provided as `Badge` (`c--badge`) from the `@lism-css/ui` package.

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
|`variant`<small>(optional)</small>| Outputs the `c--badge--{variant}` class. An `outline` style is provided by default. |

### Source Code

The source code is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/tree/main/packages/lism-ui/src/components/Badge).

    <Cluster g="15">

    ```jsx
      </Lism>

        Badge
      </Lism>
    </Cluster>
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="l--cluster -g:15">

      <span
        class="u--cbox -bd -fz:xs -hl:xs -py:5 -px:10 -bdrs:99"
        style="--keycolor: var(--blue); --bdc: color-mix(in srgb, var(--keycolor) 40%, var(--base))"
        >Badge</span
      >
    </div>
    ```

# Button.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/ui/Button.mdx

title: 'Button'
description: 'Documentation for the Button component provided by @lism-css/ui.'

import { Box, Flex, Grid, Lism, Frame, Media, Icon, Spacer, Center, Layer, Cluster, Stack, Link } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { Button } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/Button';
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';
import { ArrowRightIcon, ShoppingCartSimpleIcon } from "@phosphor-icons/react";

A component for displaying button-style links.

  <PreviewTitle>Preview</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20" bg=":stripe" layout="">
    <Flex layout="cluster" g="15">
      <Button href="###" variant="fill">
        <Fragment>Button</Fragment>
      </Button>
      <Button href="###" variant="outline">
        <Fragment>Outline</Fragment>
      </Button>
    </Flex>
  <PreviewCode slot="tab" label="React / Astro">
    ```jsx
    <Flex layout="cluster" g="15">
      <Button href="###" variant="fill">
        Button
      </Button>
      <Button href="###" variant="outline">
        Outline
      </Button>
    </Flex>
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="l--cluster -g:15">
      <a class="c--button c--button--fill l--flex -hl:s -py:10 -px:20 -hov:-o" href="###">
        {' '}
        Button{' '}
      </a>
      <a class="c--button c--button--outline l--flex -hl:s -py:10 -px:20 -hov:-o" href="###">
        Outline
      </a>
    </div>
    ```

## Usage

Provided as `Button` (`c--button`) from the `@lism-css/ui` package.

### Import

<ImportPackage component="Button" packageName="@lism-css/ui" css="style.css" />

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
|`variant`<small>(optional)</small>| Outputs the `c--button--{variant}` class. Two styles are available: `fill` and `outline`. |

### Source Code

The source code is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/tree/main/packages/lism-ui/src/components/Button).

## Examples

  <PreviewTitle>`Button` examples</PreviewTitle>

        <Icon icon="cart" />
        Button
      </Button>
    </Flex>

    ```jsx
    <Flex g="15">
      <Button href="###">Button</Button>
      <Button href="###" bgc="brand" bdrs="10">
        Button
      </Button>
      <Button href="###" bgc="#d13d5e" bdrs="99">

        Button
      </Button>
    </Flex>
    ```
    ```html

      <a class="c--button l--flex -hl:s -py:10 -px:20 -hov:-o -bgc -bdrs:99" style="--bgc: #d13d5e" href="###">

      </a>
    </div>
    ```

### Aligning icons to the edge using `Grid`

Specifying `layout='grid'` applies the `l--grid` class, enabling a grid layout where icons can be pinned to the edges of the button.

  <PreviewTitle>Preview</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20" flow="20">
    <Stack max-w="20em" g="15">
      <Button href="###" layout="grid" py="15" bdrs="10" hov="-bgc">
        <Icon icon="cart" />
        <span>Button</span>
      </Button>
      <Button href="###" layout="grid" py="15" bdrs="10" hov="-bgc">
        <span>Button</span>
        <Icon icon={ArrowRightIcon} />
      </Button>
      <Button href="###" layout="grid" py="15" bdrs="10" hov="-bgc">
        <Icon icon="cart" />
        <span>Button</span>
        <Icon icon={ArrowRightIcon} />
      </Button>
    </Stack>
    ```jsx 'layout="grid"'
    <Button href="###" layout="grid" max-w="20em" py="15" bdrs="10" hov="-bgc">
      <Icon icon="cart" />
      <span>Button</span>
    </Button>
    <Button href="###" layout="grid" max-w="20em" py="15" bdrs="10" hov="-bgc">
      <span>Button</span>
      <Icon icon={ArrowRightIcon} />
    </Button>
    <Button href="###" layout="grid" max-w="20em" py="15" bdrs="10" hov="-bgc">
      <Icon icon="cart" />
      <span>Button</span>
      <Icon icon={ArrowRightIcon} />
    </Button>
    ```

  <PreviewCode slot="tab" label="CSS">
  ```css
  .c--button:where(.l--grid) {
    grid-template-columns: minmax(1em, auto) 1fr minmax(1em, auto);
    justify-items: center;
  }
  .c--button:where(.l--grid) > :not(.a--icon) {
    grid-column: 2;
  }
  ```

## Opt-in styles

### `hov="reverse"`

An example of adding a [`-hov` class](/en/docs/property-class/hov) that swaps the fill and outline styles on hover.

<Preview css={`
.-hov\\:reverse {
  --hov-c: var(--bgc);
  --hov-bgc: var(--c);
}
.-hov\\:reverse:where(.c--button--fill) {
  --hov-bgc: transparent;
}
.-hov\\:reverse:where(.c--button--outline) {
  --hov-c: var(--base);
}
@media (any-hover: hover) {
  .-hov\\:reverse:hover {
    background-color: var(--hov-bgc) !important;
    color: var(--hov-c) !important;
  }
}`}>
  <PreviewTitle>Example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20" bg=":stripe" layout="">
    <Flex g="15">
      <Button href="###" hov="reverse" variant="fill">
        <Fragment>Button</Fragment>
      </Button>
      <Button href="###" hov="reverse" variant="outline">
        <Fragment>Button</Fragment>
      </Button>
    </Flex>

  <PreviewCode slot="tab" label="Additional CSS">
  ```scss
  .-hov\:reverse {
    --hov-c: var(--bgc);
    --hov-bgc: var(--c);
    &:where(.c--button--fill) {
      --hov-bgc: transparent;
    }
    &:where(.c--button--outline) {
      --hov-c: var(--base);
    }
    @media (any-hover: hover) {
      &:hover {
        background-color: var(--hov-bgc) !important;
        color: var(--hov-c) !important;
      }
    }
  }
  ```
  ```jsx 'hov="reverse"'
  <Flex g="15">
    <Button href="###" hov="reverse" variant="fill">
      Button
    </Button>
    <Button href="###" hov="reverse" variant="outline">
      Button
    </Button>
  </Flex>
  ```

## Without @lism-css/ui

An example of building a Button using only lism-css, without `@lism-css/ui`.

  <PreviewTitle>Preview</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20" bg=":stripe" flow="s">
    <Flex g="15">
      <Link href="###" d="inline-flex" w="fit" td="none" c="base" bgc="text" hl="s" py="10" px="20" bdrs="20" hov="-o">Button</Link>
      <Link href="###" d="inline-flex" w="fit" td="none" c="inherit" bd hl="s" py="10" px="20" bdrs="20" hov="-o">Button</Link>
    </Flex>
    <Grid
      as="a"
      href="###"
      gtc="1em 1fr 1em"
      ji="center"

# Callout.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/ui/Callout.mdx

title: 'Callout'
description: 'Documentation for the Callout component provided by @lism-css/ui.'
import { Icon, Box, Flex, Center, Lism, Stack } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { Callout } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/Callout';
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';

A component for highlighting important points within an article.

  <PreviewTitle>Preview</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="30" resize>

      <p>
        Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim
        veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris.
      </p>
    </Callout>
    <PreviewCode slot="tab" label="React / Astro">
    ```jsx
    <Callout title="Callout Title">
      <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet...</p>
    </Callout>
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="c--callout l--stack u--cbox -p:20 -g:10 -bd-s" style="--keycolor:var(--blue);--bdc:var(--keycolor);--bdw: 3px">
      <div class="l--flex -c -fw:bold -ai:center -g:10" style="--c:var(--keycolor)">
        <div class="l--center">
          <svg
            xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
            viewBox="0 0 256 256"

            height="1.25em"

            <path d="M229.66,58.34l-32-32a8,8,0,0,0-11.32,0l-96,96A8,8,0,0,0,88,128v32a8,8,0,0,0,8,8h32a8,8,0,0,0,5.66-2.34l96-96A8,8,0,0,0,229.66,58.34ZM124.69,152H104V131.31l64-64L188.69,88ZM200,76.69,179.31,56,192,43.31,212.69,64ZM224,120v88a16,16,0,0,1-16,16H48a16,16,0,0,1-16-16V48A16,16,0,0,1,48,32h88a8,8,0,0,1,0,16H48V208H208V120a8,8,0,0,1,16,0Z"></path>
    ```

## Usage

Provided as `Callout` from the `@lism-css/ui` package.

### Import
<ImportPackage component="Callout" packageName="@lism-css/ui" />

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
|`keycolor`| Specifies the display color. |
|`icon`| Specifies the icon. |
|`type`| Specifies a preset value combining `keycolor` and `icon`. Default: `"note"` |
|`title`| Specifies the title text. |
|`flow`| Passed to `_body`. |

### Source Code

The source code is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/tree/main/packages/lism-ui/src/components/Callout).

# Chat.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/ui/Chat.mdx

title: 'Chat'
description: 'Documentation for the Chat component provided by @lism-css/ui.'

import { Chat } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/Chat';
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';

A component for displaying content in a chat conversation style.

  <PreviewTitle>Preview</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="30" _dir="rtl">
    <Chat name="Taro" avatar="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-01.jpg">
      <p>
        Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim
        veniam, quis nostrud exercitation.
      </p>
    </Chat>
  <PreviewCode slot="tab" label="React / Astro">
    ```jsx
    <Chat name="Taro" avatar="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-01.jpg">
      <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet...</p>
    </Chat>
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="c--chat c--chat--speak l--grid -ji:start" style="--keycolor: var(--gray)" data-chat-dir="start">
      <div class="c--chat_avatar l--frame -bgc:base -ar:1/1 -bdrs:99" src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-01.jpg" aria-hidden="true">
        <img src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-01.jpg" alt="" width="60" height="60" decoding="async" />
      </div>
      <div class="c--chat_name -c:text-2 -fs:italic -fz:2xs -hl:0 -py:5 -px:10 -aslf:end">Taro</div>
      <div class="c--chat_body -pos:relative">
        <div class="c--chat_deco a--decorator is--skipFlow u--cbox -pos:absolute" aria-hidden="true"></div>
        <div class="c--chat_content l--flow u--cbox -flow:s -bdrs:30 -p:20 -hl:s -jslf:start">
          <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet...</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    ```

## Usage

Provided as `Chat` (`c--chat`) from the `@lism-css/ui` package.

### Import
<ImportPackage component="Chat" packageName="@lism-css/ui" css="style.css" />

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
| `avatar` | Specifies the `src` of the chat avatar image. |
| `name` | Specifies the name displayed in the chat. |
| `variant` | Specifies the chat type. Available options: `speak` or `think`. |
| `direction` | Specifies the display position of the chat. Use `start` or `end`. |
| `keycolor` | Specifies the key color of the chat bubble. |
| `flow` | Passed to the element wrapping the content (`c--chat_content`). |

### Source Code

The source code is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/tree/main/packages/lism-ui/src/components/Chat).

## Examples

  <PreviewTitle>`<Chat>` examples</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20" _dir="rtl">
    <Chat name="Taro" avatar="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-01.jpg">
      <DummyText lang="en" />
    </Chat>
    <Chat direction="end" name="Hanako" avatar="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-02.jpg" keycolor="green">
      <DummyText lang="en" length="codes" />
      <DummyText lang="en" />
    </Chat>
  <PreviewCode>
    ```jsx
    <Chat name="Taro" avatar="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-01.jpg">
      <DummyText lang="en" />
    </Chat>
    <Chat direction="end" name="Hanako" avatar="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/avatar/a-02.jpg" keycolor="green">
      <DummyText lang="en" length="codes" />
    </Chat>
    ```

}
`}>

      <DummyText length="codes" />
    </Chat>

# Details.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/ui/Details.mdx

title: 'Details'
description: 'Documentation for the Details component provided by @lism-css/ui.'

import { Divider, Stack, Center, Flex, Icon } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { Accordion } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/Accordion';
import { Details } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/Details';
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';

A UI component for creating collapsible accordion-style content using the `details`/`summary` elements.

Unlike [`Accordion`](/en/docs/ui/Accordion/), this component is implemented with CSS only — no JavaScript required.

  <PreviewTitle>Preview</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Details.Root bd>
      <Details.Summary p="20" bgc="base-2" hov="-bgc">
        <Details.Title>Details Title</Details.Title>
        <Details.Icon />
      </Details.Summary>
      <Details.Content p="20">
        <p>Content goes here.</p>
      </Details.Content>
    </Details.Root>
    ```jsx
    <Details.Root bd>
      <Details.Summary p="20" bgc="base-2" hov="-bgc">
        <Details.Title>Details Title</Details.Title>
        <Details.Icon />
      </Details.Summary>
      <Details.Content p="20">
        <p>Content goes here.</p>
      </Details.Content>
    </Details.Root>
    ```
    ```html
    <details class="c--details -bd">
      <summary class="c--details_summary l--flex -g:10 -ai:center -p:20 -bgc:base-2 -hov:-bgc">
        <span class="c--details_title -fx:1">Details Title</span>
        <span class="c--details_icon a--icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      </summary>
      <div class="c--details_body">
        <div class="c--details_content l--flow -flow:s -p:20">
          <p>Content goes here.</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </details>
    ```

## Usage

Provided as `Details` (`c--details`) from the `@lism-css/ui` package.

### Import

<ImportPackage component="Details" packageName="@lism-css/ui" css="style.css" />

The following components are available:

- `<Details.Root>`
- `<Details.Summary>`
- `<Details.Title>`
- `<Details.Icon>`
- `<Details.Content>`

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
| <PropBadge>`<Details.Root>`</PropBadge><br/>`--duration` | Duration of the expand/collapse animation. |
| <PropBadge>`<Details.Title>`</PropBadge><br/>`as` | The HTML tag used to render the title inside the summary element. |

### Structure

```jsx
<Details.Root>
  <Details.Summary>
    <Details.Title>Details Title</Details.Title>
    <Details.Icon />
  </Details.Summary>
  <Details.Content>...Contents...</Details.Content>
</Details.Root>
```

### Source Code

The source code is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/tree/main/packages/lism-ui/src/components/Details).

## Examples

### Custom title tag and exclusive expansion

`<Details.Title>` renders as a `span` by default, but you can specify an HTML tag via `as`.

Additionally, as a native feature of `details`/`summary`, adding a `name` attribute restricts the group to one open item at a time.

  <PreviewTitle>Example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Stack g="10">
      <Details.Root bd name="details-group-01">
        <Details.Summary p="20" bgc="base-2" hov="-bgc">
          <Details.Title as="h3">Details Title</Details.Title>
          <Details.Icon />
        </Details.Summary>
        <Details.Content p="20">
          <p>Content goes here.</p>
        </Details.Content>
      </Details.Root>
      <Details.Root bd name="details-group-01">
        <Details.Summary p="20" bgc="base-2" hov="-bgc">
          <Details.Title as="h3">Details Title</Details.Title>
          <Details.Icon />
        </Details.Summary>
        <Details.Content p="20">
          <p>Content goes here.</p>
        </Details.Content>
      </Details.Root>
    </Stack>
    ```jsx 'as="h3"' 'name="details-group-01"'
    <Stack g="10">
      <Details.Root bd name="details-group-01">
        <Details.Summary p="20" bgc="base-2" hov="-bgc">
          <Details.Title as="h3">Details Title</Details.Title>
          <Details.Icon />
        </Details.Summary>
        <Details.Content p="20">
          <p>Content goes here.</p>
        </Details.Content>
      </Details.Root>
      <Details.Root bd name="details-group-01">
        <Details.Summary p="20" bgc="base-2" hov="-bgc">
          <Details.Title as="h3">Details Title</Details.Title>
          <Details.Icon />
        </Details.Summary>
        <Details.Content p="20">
          <p>Content goes here.</p>
        </Details.Content>
      </Details.Root>
    </Stack>
    ```

:::warning
::title[Heading elements inside summary]
There was a known issue where screen readers could not detect the role of heading elements placed inside `summary`, but as of 2026, this has been largely resolved in modern browsers.
:::

### Animation duration

The duration of the `<Details>` open/close animation is controlled by the `--duration` variable, which defaults to the same value as `<Accordion>` — `--acc-duration`.

For local adjustments, override the `--duration` variable. For global adjustments, override `--acc-duration` on `:root`.

  <PreviewTitle>Example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Details.Root bd style={{ '--duration': '.4s' }}>
      <Details.Summary p="20" bgc="base-2" hov="-bgc">
        <Details.Icon />
        <Details.Title as="h3">Details Title</Details.Title>
      </Details.Summary>
      <Details.Content p="20">
        <p>Content goes here.</p>
      </Details.Content>
    </Details.Root>
    ```jsx "--duration"
    <Details.Root bd style={{ '--duration': '.4s' }}>
      <Details.Summary p="20" bgc="base-2" hov="-bgc">
        <Details.Title as="h3">Details Title</Details.Title>
        <Details.Icon />
      </Details.Summary>
      <Details.Content p="20">
        <p>Content goes here.</p>
      </Details.Content>
    </Details.Root>
    ```

---

# DummyText.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/ui/DummyText.mdx

title: 'DummyText'
description: 'A component for outputting dummy text for prototyping and design mockups.'
import { Stack } from "lism-css/astro";
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';

Outputs dummy placeholder text. Supports multiple languages and text lengths.

## Usage

Provided as `DummyText` from the `@lism-css/ui` package.

### Import

```jsx
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';
// or
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/react/DummyText';
```

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
| `lang` | Specifies the language. Defaults to `en`. Also supports `ja` and `ar`. |
| `length` | Specifies the length of the dummy text. Valid values are `xs`, `s`, `m`, `l`, `xl`, `codes`. Defaults to `m`. |
| `pre` | Specifies text to display before the dummy text. |
| `as` | Specifies the HTML tag. Defaults to `p`. |
| `offset` | Specifies an offset for the dummy text. Text is trimmed at `,`, `.`, `、`, and `。` boundaries, so the resulting text will be shorter. |

## Examples

  <PreviewTitle>Dummy text in different languages</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <DummyText />
    <DummyText lang="ja" />
  <PreviewCode>
    ```jsx
    <DummyText />
    <DummyText lang="ja" />
    ```

  <PreviewTitle>Dummy text at different lengths</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <DummyText length="xs" pre="xs: " />
    <DummyText length="s" pre="s: " />
    <DummyText length="m" pre="m: " />
    <DummyText length="l" pre="l: " />
    <DummyText length="xl" pre="xl: " />
  <PreviewCode>
    ```jsx
    <DummyText length="xs" pre="xs: " />
    <DummyText length="s" pre="s: " />
    <DummyText length="m" pre="m: " />
    <DummyText length="l" pre="l: " />
    <DummyText length="xl" pre="xl: " />
    ```

  <PreviewTitle>`length='codes'` — inline elements (`<b>`, `<i>`, `<a>`, `<code>`)</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <DummyText length="codes" />
  <PreviewCode>
    ```jsx
    <DummyText length="codes" />
    ```

    <DummyText length="xs" />
    <DummyText offset={1} />
    <DummyText length="l" offset={3} />
  <PreviewCode>
    ```jsx
    <DummyText length="xs" />
    <DummyText offset={1} />
    <DummyText length="l" offset={3} />
    ```

# Modal.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/ui/Modal.mdx

title: 'Modal'
description: 'Documentation for the Modal component provided by @lism-css/ui.'

import { Grid, Flex, Stack, Center, Icon, Inline, Link } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { Modal } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/Modal';
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';

A component for displaying modals using the `dialog` element.

## Usage

Provided as `Modal` from the `@lism-css/ui` package.

### Import

<ImportPackage component="Modal" script="modal.js" packageName="@lism-css/ui" />

`<Modal.Root>`, `<Modal.Inner>`, `<Modal.Body>`, and `<Modal.CloseBtn>` are available.

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
|`id`| The `id` attribute is required on Modal (`c--modal`). |
|<PropBadge>`<Modal.Root>`</PropBadge><br/> `duration`| Sets the duration of the modal open/close animation. Output as the `--duration` variable. |
|<PropBadge>`<Modal.Inner>`</PropBadge><br/> `layout`| Specifies the layout component for `__inner`. |
|<PropBadge>`<Modal.Inner>`</PropBadge><br/> `offset`| Offset value to shift the position of `__inner` when hidden. |
|<PropBadge>`<Modal.OpenBtn>`</PropBadge><br/> `modalId`| Output as `data-modal-open`. Specifies the modal `id` on the trigger element that opens the modal. |
|<PropBadge>`<Modal.CloseBtn>`</PropBadge><br/> `modalId`| Output as `data-modal-close`. Specifies the modal `id` on the trigger element that closes the modal. |

### Structure

```jsx
<Modal.OpenBtn modalId="modalID">Open</Modal.OpenBtn>
<Modal.Root id="modalID">
  <Modal.Inner>
    <Modal.Body>...Contents...</Modal.Body>
    <Modal.CloseBtn modalId="modalID" />
  </Modal.Inner>
</Modal.Root>
```

Add an `id` to `<Modal.Root>`, and pass the same `modalId` to `<Modal.OpenBtn>` / `<Modal.CloseBtn>` to wire up the open/close triggers.

### Source Code

The source code is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/tree/main/packages/lism-ui/src/components/Modal).

## Examples

- Do not change the `display` value of the `dialog` element.
- Due to animation issues with `::backdrop`, this component assumes the dialog covers the full viewport width with a background color.

  <PreviewTitle>Modal usage example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="30">
    <Modal.OpenBtn modalId="modal-01" className="-bd -px:15 -py:5 -bdrs:10">
      <Fragment>Open Modal 01</Fragment>
    </Modal.OpenBtn>

    <Modal.Root id="modal-01" isWrapper isContainer p="30">
      <Modal.Inner layout="stack" pos="relative" p="30" bdrs="20" bxsh="40">
        <Modal.CloseBtn modalId="modal-01" autofocus pos="absolute" t="0" r="0" z="1" fz="xl" p="10" m="15" />
        <Modal.Body layout="stack" g="30" util="trimAll">
          <div className="-fz:xl -fw:bold">Modal Title</div>
          <DummyText />
        </Modal.Body>
      </Modal.Inner>
    </Modal.Root>
    ```jsx '"modal-01"'
    <Modal.OpenBtn modalId="modal-01" className="-bd -px:15 -py:5 -bdrs:10">Open Modal 01</Modal.OpenBtn>

    <Modal.Root id="modal-01" isWrapper isContainer p="30">
      <Modal.Inner layout="stack" pos="relative" p="30" bdrs="20" bxsh="40">
        <Modal.CloseBtn modalId="modal-01" autofocus pos="absolute" t="0" r="0" z="1" fz="xl" p="10" m="15" />
        <Modal.Body layout="stack" g="30" util="trimAll">
          <div className="-fz:xl -fw:bold">Modal Title</div>
          <DummyText />
        </Modal.Body>
      </Modal.Inner>
    </Modal.Root>
    ```
    ```html
    ```

# NavMenu.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/ui/NavMenu.mdx

title: 'NavMenu'
description: 'Documentation for the NavMenu component provided by @lism-css/ui.'
import { Lism, Icon, Spacer, Box } from 'lism-css/astro'
import { Accordion } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/Accordion';
import { NavMenu } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/NavMenu';

A component for creating navigation menu lists.

## Usage

Provided as `NavMenu` (`c--navMenu`) from the `@lism-css/ui` package.

### Import

<ImportPackage component="NavMenu" packageName="@lism-css/ui" css="style.css" />

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
| <PropBadge>`<NavMenu.Root>`</PropBadge><br/>`hovBgc` | Outputs `--hov-bgc`. (For use when `-hov:-bgc` is applied to `c--navMenu_link`.) |
| <PropBadge>`<NavMenu.Root>`</PropBadge><br/>`hovC` | Outputs `--hov-c`. (For use when `-hov:-c` is applied to `c--navMenu_link`.) |
| <PropBadge>`<NavMenu.Root>`</PropBadge><br/>`itemP` | Outputs the `--_item-p` variable. Adjusts the padding of each link at once. |
| <PropBadge>`<NavMenu.Link>`</PropBadge><br/>`hov` | Specifies the hover style. Defaults to `-bgc`, changing the background color on hover. |

### Structure

```jsx
<NavMenu.Root>
  <NavMenu.Item>
    <NavMenu.Link href="">Menu item</NavMenu.Link>
  </NavMenu.Item>
  <NavMenu.Item>
    <NavMenu.Link href="">Menu item</NavMenu.Link>
    <NavMenu.Nest>
      <NavMenu.Item>
        <NavMenu.Link href="">Nested item</NavMenu.Link>
      </NavMenu.Item>
    </NavMenu.Nest>
  </NavMenu.Item>
</NavMenu.Root>
```

Use `<NavMenu.Nest>` to create nested menus.

### Source Code

The source code is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/tree/main/packages/lism-ui/src/components/NavMenu).

## Examples

### Simple example
  <PreviewTitle>Example</PreviewTitle>

        <NavMenu.Link href="#menu">
          <Fragment>Menu item 1</Fragment>
        </NavMenu.Link>
      </NavMenu.Item>
      <NavMenu.Item>
        <NavMenu.Link href="#menu">
          <Fragment>Menu item 2</Fragment>
        </NavMenu.Link>
      </NavMenu.Item>
      <NavMenu.Item>
        <NavMenu.Link href="#menu">
          <Fragment>Menu item 3</Fragment>
        </NavMenu.Link>
      </NavMenu.Item>
    </NavMenu.Root>
  <PreviewCode>
    ```jsx

    </NavMenu.Root>
    ```

### Setting common styles for all items at once

Some props can be specified on `NavMenu.Root` and applied to all links at once, instead of setting them directly on each `NavMenu.Link`.

- `itemP` adjusts the padding (`--_item-p`) of each `NavMenu.Link`.
- `hovBgc` provides the hover background color (`--hov-bgc`). (Requires `-hov:-bgc` on `NavMenu.Link`.)
- `hovC` provides the hover text color (`--hov-c`). (Requires `-hov:-c` on `NavMenu.Link`.)

To change the padding per breakpoint, set `p` on each `<NavMenu.Link>` instead of using `itemP`.

  <PreviewTitle>Common styles on the Root</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="30">
    <NavMenu.Root bd itemP="30" hovBgc="text" hovC="base">
      <NavMenu.Item>
        <NavMenu.Link href="#menu1" hov="-bgc,-c">Menu item</NavMenu.Link>
      </NavMenu.Item>
      <NavMenu.Item bd-t>
        <NavMenu.Link href="#menu2" hov="-bgc,-c">Menu item</NavMenu.Link>
      </NavMenu.Item>
      <NavMenu.Item bd-t>
        <NavMenu.Link href="#menu3" hov="-bgc,-c">Menu item</NavMenu.Link>
      </NavMenu.Item>
    </NavMenu.Root>
  <PreviewCode>
    ```jsx 'itemP="30"' 'hovBgc="text"' 'hovC="base"'
    <NavMenu.Root bd itemP="30" hovBgc="text" hovC="base">
      <NavMenu.Item>
        <NavMenu.Link href="#menu1" hov="-bgc,-c">Menu item</NavMenu.Link>
      </NavMenu.Item>
      <NavMenu.Item bd-t>
        <NavMenu.Link href="#menu2" hov="-bgc,-c">Menu item</NavMenu.Link>
      </NavMenu.Item>
      <NavMenu.Item bd-t>
        <NavMenu.Link href="#menu3" hov="-bgc,-c">Menu item</NavMenu.Link>
      </NavMenu.Item>
    </NavMenu.Root>
    ```

### Expanding nested menus with an accordion

Since link padding is managed by `--_item-p`, you can use `var(--_item-p)` inside an accordion to apply the same padding amount.

  <PreviewTitle>Example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <NavMenu.Root bd-y hovBgc="base-2">
      <NavMenu.Item>
        <NavMenu.Link href="#menu1">
          <Fragment>Menu item</Fragment>
        </NavMenu.Link>
      </NavMenu.Item>
      <NavMenu.Item>
        <Accordion.Root>
          <Accordion.Item>
            <Accordion.Heading>
              <Accordion.Button hov="-bgc" p="var(--_item-p)">
                <Fragment>Menu item (Accordion)</Fragment>
              </Accordion.Button>
            </Accordion.Heading>
            <Accordion.Panel>
              <NavMenu.Nest>
                <NavMenu.Item>
                  <NavMenu.Link href="#child-menu1">
                    <Fragment>Nested item</Fragment>
                  </NavMenu.Link>
                </NavMenu.Item>
                <NavMenu.Item>
                  <NavMenu.Link href="#child-menu2">
                    <Fragment>Nested item</Fragment>
                  </NavMenu.Link>
                </NavMenu.Item>
              </NavMenu.Nest>
            </Accordion.Panel>
          </Accordion.Item>
        </Accordion.Root>
      </NavMenu.Item>
    </NavMenu.Root>
  <PreviewCode>
    ```jsx "Accordion.Root" "NavMenu.Nest"
    <NavMenu.Root bd-y hovBgc="base-2">
      <NavMenu.Item>

          Menu item

                Menu item (Accordion)

                    Nested item
                  </NavMenu.Link>
    ```

### Horizontal menu with hover-revealed submenu

    ```jsx 'fxd="row"'
        </NavMenu.Item>
        <NavMenu.Item>
          <NavMenu.Link href="#menu1" hov="-o">Menu item</NavMenu.Link>
        </NavMenu.Item>
      </NavMenu.Root>
    </Box>
    ```

# ShapeDivider.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/ui/ShapeDivider.mdx

title: 'ShapeDivider'
description: 'Documentation for the ShapeDivider component provided by @lism-css/ui.'

import { Box, Wrapper, Container, Divider, Frame, Spacer, Layer, Media, Stack } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { ShapeDivider } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/ShapeDivider';
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';

A component that renders a decorative border using SVG.

  <PreviewTitle>Preview</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize layout="">
    <Stack>
      <ShapeDivider isEmpty level="2" />
      <DummyText p="30" />
      <ShapeDivider viewBox="0 0 100 10">
        <path d="M100 6C89.3 3.3 82.7 9 70 9S48.4 3 38 3 24.5 6 17 6C7.4 6 0 0 0 0v10h100V6z" />
      </ShapeDivider>
    </Stack>

## Usage

Provided as `ShapeDivider` (`c--shapeDivider`) from the `@lism-css/ui` package.

### Import

<ImportPackage component="ShapeDivider" packageName="@lism-css/ui" css="style.css" />

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
| `viewBox` | The `viewBox` attribute for the output SVG. |
| `level` | Specifies the height level of the shape as a positive number. Default is `5`. |
| `offset` | Outputs a variable to shift the shape horizontally. |
| `stretch` | Outputs a variable to stretch the shape horizontally. |
| `isEmpty` | Renders no shape, allowing the component to be used as a spacer. |
| `isAnimation` | Enables animation. Outputs `data-has-animation="true"`. |

### Source Code

The source code is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/tree/main/packages/lism-ui/src/components/ShapeDivider).

## Examples

### Placing shapes at the top and bottom of a section

Use `flip` to mirror the shape, allowing you to reuse the same SVG path for both the top and bottom dividers. (Separate paths can be provided instead if preferred.)

  <PreviewTitle>Preview</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="0" layout="">
    <Wrapper hasGutter py="40">
      <DummyText />
    </Wrapper>
    <ShapeDivider viewBox="0 0 10 10" level="4">
      <path d="M10,10V0L0,9.5V10L10,10z"></path>
    </ShapeDivider>
    <Wrapper hasGutter bgc="text" c="base">
      <Box py="40">
        <DummyText length="l" />
      </Box>
    </Wrapper>
    <ShapeDivider viewBox="0 0 10 10" level="4" flip="XY">
      <path d="M10,10V0L0,9.5V10L10,10z"></path>
    </ShapeDivider>
    <Wrapper hasGutter py="40">
      <DummyText />
    </Wrapper>
    ```jsx "\<ShapeDivider" "\/ShapeDivider\>" 'flip="XY"'
    <Wrapper hasGutter py="40">
      <DummyText />
    </Wrapper>
    <ShapeDivider viewBox="0 0 10 10" level="4">
      <path d="M10,10V0L0,9.5V10L10,10z"></path>
    </ShapeDivider>
    <Wrapper hasGutter bgc="text" c="base">
      <Box py="40">
        <DummyText length="l" />
      </Box>
    </Wrapper>
    <ShapeDivider viewBox="0 0 10 10" level="4" flip="XY">
      <path d="M10,10V0L0,9.5V10L10,10z"></path>
    </ShapeDivider>
    <Wrapper hasGutter py="40">
      <DummyText />
    </Wrapper>
    ```

### Using an empty ShapeDivider as a spacer

You can use the component as a spacer by omitting the path and specifying `isEmpty`.

Even when empty, `level` still controls the height, making it useful for managing spacing on the side opposite a shape divider.

  <PreviewTitle>Preview</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="0" layout="">
    <Wrapper hasGutter bgc="base">
      <ShapeDivider isEmpty level="5" />
      <Box py="20">
        <DummyText length="l" />
      </Box>
      <ShapeDivider viewBox="0 0 10 10" level="5">
        <path d="M10,10V0L0,9.5V10L10,10z"></path>
      </ShapeDivider>
    </Wrapper>
    <Wrapper hasGutter bgc="text" c="base">
      <Box py="40">
        <DummyText length="l" />
      </Box>
    </Wrapper>
    ```jsx "isEmpty" 'level="5"'
    <Wrapper hasGutter bgc="base">
      <ShapeDivider isEmpty level="5" />
      <Box py="20">
        <DummyText length="l" />
      </Box>
      <ShapeDivider viewBox="0 0 10 10" level="5" >
        <path d="M10,10V0L0,9.5V10L10,10z"></path>
      </ShapeDivider>
    </Wrapper>
    <Wrapper hasGutter bgc="text" c="base">
      <Box py="40">
        <DummyText length="l" />
      </Box>
    </Wrapper>
    ```

<Spacer h="1rem"/>

An example with animation enabled using `isAnimation`.

  <PreviewTitle>Preview</PreviewTitle>

      <ShapeDivider isEmpty level="7" />

        <Media src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-1.jpg" alt="" width="960" height="640" />

      </Frame>
      <Wrapper contentSize="s" py="40" c="white">
        <DummyText length="l" />

        <path opacity=".3" d="M100,1.5C87.8,6.6,79.3,2.1,67.8,2.6S53,6.5,42.5,5.5S23,0,15,0S1,3,0,4v6h100V1.5z"></path>
        <path d="M100,7.5C91.5,5,77.1,11.8,54,8C34.6,4.8,14.4,4.1,0,8.5V10h100V7.5z"></path>

    </Container>
    <Container isWrapper="s" hasGutter bgc="base" py="40">

    </Container>
    ```jsx "isAnimation"

        <path d="M100,7.5C91.5,5,77.1,11.8,54,8C34.6,4.8,14.4,4.1,0,8.5V10h100V7.5z"></path>
    ```

<Spacer h="1rem"/>

### Adjusting position with `stretch` and `offset`

When reusing the same shape at both the top and bottom, simply flipping it may look slightly off.
In such cases, using `stretch` and `offset` to shift the SVG can produce a more natural result with the same shape.

  <PreviewTitle>Using `stretch` and `offset`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="0" layout="">
    <Container isWrapper="s" hasGutter bgc="base" py="40">
      <ShapeDivider isEmpty level="4" />
      <DummyText length="l" />
    </Container>
    <Container pos="relative" hasGutter c="base" bgc="text">
      <ShapeDivider viewBox="0 0 100 10" c="base" flip="Y" level="8" stretch="1.1" offset="-5%">
        <path d="M100 6C89.3 3.3 82.7 9 70 9S48.4 3 38 3 24.5 6 17 6C7.4 6 0 0 0 0v10h100V6z"></path>
      </ShapeDivider>
      <Wrapper contentSize="s" py="40">
        <DummyText length="xl" />
      </Wrapper>
      <ShapeDivider viewBox="0 0 100 10" c="base" level="8" stretch="1.1">
        <path d="M100 6C89.3 3.3 82.7 9 70 9S48.4 3 38 3 24.5 6 17 6C7.4 6 0 0 0 0v10h100V6z"></path>
      </ShapeDivider>
    </Container>
    <Container isWrapper="s" hasGutter bgc="base" py="40">
      <DummyText length="l" />
      <ShapeDivider isEmpty level="4" />
    </Container>
    ```jsx "stretch=" "offset="
    <Container isWrapper="s" hasGutter bgc="base" py="40">
      <ShapeDivider isEmpty level="4" />
      <DummyText length="l" />
    </Container>
    <Container pos="relative" hasGutter c="base" bgc="text">
      <ShapeDivider viewBox="0 0 100 10" c="base" flip="Y" level="8" stretch="1.1" offset="-5%">
        <path d="M100 6C89.3 3.3 82.7 9 70 9S48.4 3 38 3 24.5 6 17 6C7.4 6 0 0 0 0v10h100V6z"></path>
      </ShapeDivider>
      <Wrapper contentSize="s" py="40">
        <DummyText length="xl" />
      </Wrapper>
      <ShapeDivider viewBox="0 0 100 10" c="base" level="8" stretch="1.1">
        <path d="M100 6C89.3 3.3 82.7 9 70 9S48.4 3 38 3 24.5 6 17 6C7.4 6 0 0 0 0v10h100V6z"></path>
      </ShapeDivider>
    </Container>
    <Container isWrapper="s" hasGutter bgc="base" py="40">
      <DummyText length="l" />
      <ShapeDivider isEmpty level="4" />
    </Container>
    ```

# Tabs.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/ui/Tabs.mdx

title: 'Tabs'
description: 'Documentation for the Tabs component provided by @lism-css/ui.'

import { Icon } from 'lism-css/astro';
import { Tabs } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/Tabs';
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';
import '../../ja/ui/_opt-in/_tabs-line.css'
import '../../ja/ui/_opt-in/_tabs-emboss.css'
import '../../ja/ui/_opt-in/_tabs-keep-height.css'

A component for creating tab elements.
Only interaction behavior is provided — visual styling is intentionally left for you to customize.

## Usage

Provided as `Tabs` from the `@lism-css/ui` package.

### Import

<ImportPackage component="Tabs" script="tabs.js" packageName="@lism-css/ui" />

### Props

| Prop | Description |
|---|---|
|<PropBadge>`<Tabs.Root>`</PropBadge><br/>`variant`| Outputs the `c--tabs--{variant}` class. |
|<PropBadge>`<Tabs.Root>`</PropBadge><br/>`tabId`| A string ID used as the value for `aria-controls` to identify each tab. |
|<PropBadge>`<Tabs.Root>`</PropBadge><br/>`defaultIndex`| Specifies which tab to open initially. |
|<PropBadge>`<Tabs.Root>`</PropBadge><br/>`listProps`| Props passed to the list element (`c--tabs_list`) wrapping the tab buttons. |

### Structure

```jsx
<Tabs.Root>
  <Tabs.Item>
    <Tabs.Tab>Tab label</Tabs.Tab>
    <Tabs.Panel>...Contents...</Tabs.Panel>
  </Tabs.Item>
</Tabs.Root>
```

:::warning
Only `<Tabs.Tab>` and `<Tabs.Panel>` are recognized as children of `<Tabs.Item>`. Both must always be used together.
:::

### Source Code

The source code is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/tree/main/packages/lism-ui/src/components/Tabs).

## Examples

### Basic example
  <PreviewTitle>Example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="30">
    <Tabs.Root>
      <Tabs.Item>
        <Tabs.Tab>Tab 1</Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Panel>
          <DummyText pre="Tab 01: " />
        </Tabs.Panel>
      </Tabs.Item>
      <Tabs.Item>
        <Tabs.Tab>Tab 2</Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Panel>
          <DummyText length="l" offset={1} pre="Tab 02: " />
        </Tabs.Panel>
      </Tabs.Item>
    </Tabs.Root>
    ```jsx
    <Tabs.Root>
      <Tabs.Item>
        <Tabs.Tab>Tab 1</Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Panel>
          <DummyText pre="Tab 01: " />
        </Tabs.Panel>
      </Tabs.Item>
      <Tabs.Item>
        <Tabs.Tab>Tab 2</Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Panel>
          <DummyText length="l" offset={1} pre="Tab 02: " />
        </Tabs.Panel>
      </Tabs.Item>
    </Tabs.Root>
    ```
    ```html
    ```

### Default open tab

Use `defaultIndex` on `<Tabs.Root>` to specify which tab is open by default.
(Index numbers start from `1`.)

  <PreviewTitle>Example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="30">
    <Tabs.Root defaultIndex={2}>
      <Tabs.Item>
        <Tabs.Tab>Tab 1</Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Panel>
          <DummyText pre="Tab 01: " />
        </Tabs.Panel>
      </Tabs.Item>
      <Tabs.Item>
        <Tabs.Tab>Tab 2</Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Panel>
          <DummyText length="l" offset={1} pre="Tab 02: " />
        </Tabs.Panel>
      </Tabs.Item>
    </Tabs.Root>
    ```jsx "defaultIndex=\{2\}"
    <Tabs.Root defaultIndex={2}>
      <Tabs.Item>
        <Tabs.Tab>Tab 1</Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Panel>
          <DummyText pre="Tab 01: " />
        </Tabs.Panel>
      </Tabs.Item>
      <Tabs.Item>
        <Tabs.Tab>Tab 2</Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Panel>
          <DummyText length="l" offset={1} pre="Tab 02: " />
        </Tabs.Panel>
      </Tabs.Item>
    </Tabs.Root>
    ```

### Side-by-side tab layout

Setting `grid-template: 'list panel' auto / auto 1fr;` on `<Tabs.Root>` (`c--tabs`) places the tab list and content side by side.

At the same time, changing the tab list (`c--tabs_list`) buttons to stack vertically (`flex-direction: column;`) achieves the following layout.

  <PreviewTitle>Example: side-by-side layout on `@sm` and above</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="30" resize>
    <Tabs.Root gt={[null, '"list panel" auto / auto 1fr']} listProps={{ fxd: [null, 'column'] }}>
      <Tabs.Item>
        <Tabs.Tab>
          <Fragment>Tab 1</Fragment>
        </Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Panel>
          <DummyText pre="Tab 01: " />
        </Tabs.Panel>
      </Tabs.Item>
      <Tabs.Item>
        <Tabs.Tab>
          <Fragment>Tab 2</Fragment>
        </Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Panel>
          <DummyText length="l" offset={1} pre="Tab 02: " />
        </Tabs.Panel>
      </Tabs.Item>
    </Tabs.Root>
  <PreviewCode>
    ```jsx
    <Tabs.Root gt={[null, '"list panel" auto / auto 1fr']} listProps={{ fxd: [null, 'column'] }}>
      <Tabs.Item>
        <Tabs.Tab>Tab 1</Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Panel>
          <DummyText pre="Tab 01: " />
        </Tabs.Panel>
      </Tabs.Item>
      <Tabs.Item>
        <Tabs.Tab>Tab 2</Tabs.Tab>
        <Tabs.Panel>
          <DummyText length="l" offset={1} pre="Tab 02: " />
        </Tabs.Panel>
      </Tabs.Item>
    </Tabs.Root>
    ```

# utility-class.mdx

Source: https://github.com/lism-css/lism-css/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/en/utility-class.mdx

title: 'Utility Class'
description: 'Learn about the utility classes in Lism CSS that apply bundled styles and decorations.'
import { Lism, Flow, Grid, AutoColumns, Columns, Stack, Center, Box, Media, Frame, Flex, Layer, Spacer, Icon, Divider, Inline, Text } from "lism-css/astro";
import { DummyText } from '@lism-css/ui/astro/DummyText';
import { Dog, Cat } from "@phosphor-icons/react";

This page covers the utility classes available in Lism CSS — classes that bundle a set of styles or decorations into a single class name.

## `u--cbox`

Generates `--c`, `--bgc`, and `--bdc` from the `--keycolor` variable using `color-mix()`.

`color` and `background-color` are set to the generated variables respectively, but `--bdc` is only defined as a variable — to display a border, use it together with the [`-bd` class](/en/docs/property-class/bd/).

<SrcCode path="src/scss/utility/_cbox.scss" />

  <PreviewTitle>Example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <Lism util="cbox" keycolor="red" p="20">
      <DummyText length="codes" />
    </Lism>
    <Lism util="cbox" keycolor="purple" bd bdrs="20" bxsh="20" set="bxsh" p="20">
      <DummyText length="codes" />
    </Lism>
    <Lism util="cbox" keycolor="brand" bdc="keycolor" bd-s bdw="4px" p="20">
      <DummyText length="codes" />
    </Lism>
    ```html
    <div class="u--cbox -p:20" style="--keycolor: var(--red)">
      <p>
        Lorem ipsum dolor <i>sit amet</i>. consectetur <a href="###">adipisicing elit</a>, sed do eiusmod tempor. Non facere <code>Laudantium</code> ex
        eos <b>doloribus aut dolore</b> nisi provident.
      </p>
    </div>
    <div class="set--bxsh u--cbox -bd -bdrs:20 -bxsh:20 -p:20" style="--keycolor: var(--purple)">
      <p>
        Lorem ipsum dolor <i>sit amet</i>. consectetur <a href="###">adipisicing elit</a>, sed do eiusmod tempor. Non facere <code>Laudantium</code> ex
        eos <b>doloribus aut dolore</b> nisi provident.
      </p>
    </div>
    <div class="u--cbox -bd-s -p:20" style="--keycolor: var(--brand); --bdc: var(--keycolor); --bdw: 4px">
      <p>
        Lorem ipsum dolor <i>sit amet</i>. consectetur <a href="###">adipisicing elit</a>, sed do eiusmod tempor. Non facere <code>Laudantium</code> ex
        eos <b>doloribus aut dolore</b> nisi provident.
      </p>
    </div>
    ```
    ```jsx
    <Lism util="cbox" keycolor="blue" p="20"><p>Lorem ipsum dolor <i>sit amet</i>. consectetur <a href="###">adipisicing elit</a>, sed do eiusmod tempor. Non facere <code>Laudantium</code> ex eos <b>doloribus aut dolore</b> nisi provident.</p></Lism>
    <Lism util="cbox" keycolor="red" bd p="20"><p>Lorem ipsum dolor <i>sit amet</i>. consectetur <a href="###">adipisicing elit</a>, sed do eiusmod tempor. Non facere <code>Laudantium</code> ex eos <b>doloribus aut dolore</b> nisi provident.</p></Lism>
    <Lism util="cbox" keycolor="purple" bd bdc="keycolor:base:25%" p="20"><p>Lorem ipsum dolor <i>sit amet</i>. consectetur <a href="###">adipisicing elit</a>, sed do eiusmod tempor. Non facere <code>Laudantium</code> ex eos <b>doloribus aut dolore</b> nisi provident.</p></Lism>
    <Lism util="cbox" keycolor="#688f04" bd-s bdw="4px" p="20"><p>Lorem ipsum dolor <i>sit amet</i>. consectetur <a href="###">adipisicing elit</a>, sed do eiusmod tempor. Non facere <code>Laudantium</code> ex eos <b>doloribus aut dolore</b> nisi provident.</p></Lism>
    ```

  <PreviewTitle>Badge usage example and variable customization</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <Lism layout="cluster" g="10">
      <Lism as="span" util="cbox" keycolor="red" bd fz="s" hl="s" py="5" px="10" bdrs="99">
        <Fragment>Badge</Fragment>
      </Lism>
      <Lism as="span" util="cbox" keycolor="green" bd fz="s" hl="s" py="5" px="10" bdrs="99">
        <Fragment>Badge</Fragment>
      </Lism>

      </Lism>
    </Lism>
    <Lism layout="cluster" g="10" style={{ '--cbox-cPct': '76%', '--cbox-bdPct': '20%' }}>



## `u--trim` & `u--trimAll`

Classes for adjusting the half-leading spacing of text.

`u--trim` adjusts only the element's own `margin-block`, while `u--trimAll` trims the block margins of all text-like direct children in one go.

  <PreviewTitle>`u--trim`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <Box bd bds="dashed">
      <DummyText util="trim" length="s" />
    </Box>
    ```html "u--trim"
    <div class="l--box -bd" style="--bds: dashed">
      <p class="u--trim">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipisicing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor.</p>
    </div>
    ```
    ```jsx "u--trim"
    <Box bd bds="dashed">
      <Text util="trim">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor Incididunt ut.</Text>
    </Box>
    ```
  <PreviewCode slot="tab" label="CSS">
    <SrcCode path="src/scss/utility/_trim.scss" />

`u--trimAll` uses an exclusion approach: it applies margin adjustment to all direct children except those that shouldn't be trimmed (`:empty`, `figure`, `picture`, `video`, `button`, `textarea`, `table`). The `:empty` pseudo-class automatically covers void elements like `img`, `hr`, `br`, as well as empty decorative divs (e.g. `a--divider`, `a--spacer`). If you need to exclude additional elements, add a rule like `.u--trimAll > xxx { margin-block: 0 }` on the consumer side.

  <PreviewTitle>`u--trimAll`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <Stack util="trimAll" bd g="30" p="30" bdrs="10" max-sz="s">
      <Media ar="og" src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-1.jpg" alt="" inferSize />
      <DummyText length="s" fw="bold" fz="l" />
      <DummyText length="l" o="p" fz="s" />
    </Stack>
    ```html
    <div class="l--stack u--trimAll -bd -g:30 -p:30 -bdrs:10">
      <img class="-ar:og" src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-1.jpg" />
      <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.</p>
      <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.</p>
    </div>
    ```
    ```jsx
    <Stack util="trimAll" bd g="30" p="30" bdrs="10">
      <Media ar="og" src="https://cdn.lism-css.com/img/a-1.jpg" alt="" inferSize />
      <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor Incididunt ut.</p>
      <p>
        Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor Incididunt ut. Labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim
        veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut.
      </p>
    </Stack>
    ```

## `u--srOnly`

Visually hides an element while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

<SrcCode path="src/scss/utility/_srOnly.scss" />

## `u--divide` & `u--enclose`

- `u--divide` displays dividing lines between children of a grid or flexbox container.
- `u--enclose` wraps each child in a border so they look like cells in a table.

<SrcCode path="src/scss/utility/_divide.scss" />

:::info
- Both are implemented using `box-shadow` (not actual borders), so some care is needed when using them.
- `u--divide` applies `overflow: clip` internally. Be aware that descendant elements intended to overflow the container — such as tooltips or dropdowns — will be unintentionally clipped.
:::

  <PreviewTitle>Comparing `u--divide` and `u--enclose`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <AutoColumns util="divide" cols="16rem" bdrs="20">
      <Box p="15">divide</Box>
      <Box p="15">divide</Box>
      <Box p="15">divide</Box>
      <Box p="15">divide</Box>
      <Box p="15">divide</Box>
    </AutoColumns>
    <AutoColumns util="enclose" cols="16rem" bdrs="20">
      <Box p="15">enclose</Box>
      <Box p="15">enclose</Box>
      <Box p="15">enclose</Box>
      <Box p="15">enclose</Box>
      <Box p="15">enclose</Box>
    </AutoColumns>
  ```html "u--divide" "u--enclose"
  <div class="l--autoColumns u--divide -bdrs:20" style="--cols:16rem">
    <div class="l--box -p:15">divide</div>
    <div class="l--box -p:15">divide</div>
    <div class="l--box -p:15">divide</div>
    <div class="l--box -p:15">divide</div>
    <div class="l--box -p:15">divide</div>
  </div>
  <div class="l--autoColumns u--enclose -bdrs:20" style="--cols:16rem">
    <div class="l--box -p:15">enclose</div>
    <div class="l--box -p:15">enclose</div>
    <div class="l--box -p:15">enclose</div>
    <div class="l--box -p:15">enclose</div>
    <div class="l--box -p:15">enclose</div>
  </div>
  ```
    ```jsx 'util="divide"' 'util="enclose"'
    <AutoColumns util="divide" cols="16rem" bdrs="20">
      <Box p="15">divide</Box>
      <Box p="15">divide</Box>
      <Box p="15">divide</Box>
      <Box p="15">divide</Box>
      <Box p="15">divide</Box>
    </AutoColumns>
    <AutoColumns util="enclose" cols="16rem" bdrs="20">
      <Box p="15">enclose</Box>
      <Box p="15">enclose</Box>
      <Box p="15">enclose</Box>
      <Box p="15">enclose</Box>
      <Box p="15">enclose</Box>
    </AutoColumns>
    ```

`u--divide` lets you show dividers between items in layouts that switch between horizontal and vertical.

  <PreviewTitle>Example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <Flex fxd={['column', 'row']} util="divide">
      <Lism fx="1" p="15">Item</Lism>
      <Lism fx="1" p="15">Item</Lism>
      <Lism fx="1" p="15">Item</Lism>
      <Lism fx="1" p="15">Item</Lism>
    </Flex>
    ```html "u--divide"
    <div class="l--flex u--divide -fxd:column -fxd_sm" style="--fxd_sm:row">
      <div class="-fx:1 -p:15">Item</div>
      <div class="-fx:1 -p:15">Item</div>
      <div class="-fx:1 -p:15">Item</div>
      <div class="-fx:1 -p:15">Item</div>
    </div>
    ```
    ```jsx
    <Flex fxd={['column', 'row']} util="divide">
      <Lism fx="1" p="15">Item</Lism>
      <Lism fx="1" p="15">Item</Lism>
      <Lism fx="1" p="15">Item</Lism>
      <Lism fx="1" p="15">Item</Lism>
    </Flex>
    ```

Adding `bd` to a grid with `u--divide` produces a calendar-like layout where empty cells are blank.

  <PreviewTitle>With `bd` applied</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="20">
    <Columns util="divide" cols={["4", "5"]} bd bdc="current" fz="s">
      <Lism p="10">Item</Lism>
      <Lism p="10">Item</Lism>
      <Lism p="10">Item</Lism>
      <Lism p="10">Item</Lism>
      <Lism p="10">Item</Lism>
      <Lism p="10">Item</Lism>
    </Columns>
    ```html
    <div class="l--columns u--divide -cols_sm -bd -bdc:current -fz:s" style="--cols:4;--cols_sm:5">
      <div class="-p:10">Item</div>
      <div class="-p:10">Item</div>
      <div class="-p:10">Item</div>
      <div class="-p:10">Item</div>
      <div class="-p:10">Item</div>
      <div class="-p:10">Item</div>
    </div>
    ```
    ```jsx
    <Columns util="divide" cols={["4", "5"]} bd bdc="current" fz="s">
      <Lism p="10">Item</Lism>
      <Lism p="10">Item</Lism>
      <Lism p="10">Item</Lism>
      <Lism p="10">Item</Lism>
      <Lism p="10">Item</Lism>
      <Lism p="10">Item</Lism>
    </Columns>
    ```

With Grid, `u--enclose` can be used to create a table-like layout.
  <PreviewTitle>Table-like layout using `u--enclose`</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea resize p="15">
    <Grid gtc={['2fr 3fr', '1fr 2fr']} util="enclose">
      <Box p="15" bgc="base-2">A</Box>
      <Box p="15" bgc="base-2">B</Box>
      <Box p="15">Lorem ipsum</Box>
      <Box p="15">
        <DummyText />
      </Box>
      <Box p="15">Dolor sit amet</Box>
      <Box p="15">
        <DummyText length="l" />
      </Box>
    </Grid>
    ```jsx
    <Grid gtc={['2fr 3fr', '1fr 2fr']} util="enclose">
      <Box p="15" bgc="base-2">A</Box>
      <Box p="15" bgc="base-2">B</Box>
      <Box p="15">Lorem ipsum</Box>
      <Box p="15">
        <p>
          Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor Incididunt ut. Labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim
          veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut.
        </p>
      </Box>
      <Box p="15">Dolor sit amet</Box>
      <Box p="15">
        <p>
          Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. Consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor Incididunt ut. Labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim
          veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut. Aliquip ex ea commodo consequat. Duis aute irure dolor in reprehenderit in voluptate
          velit esse cillum dolore eu fugiat nulla pariatur. Excepteur sint.
        </p>
      </Box>
    </Grid>
    ```
    ```html
    <div class="l--grid u--enclose -gtc -gtc_sm -bd" style="--gtc: 2fr 3fr; --gtc_sm: 1fr 2fr">
      <div class="l--box -p:15 -bgc:base-2">A</div>
      <div class="l--box -p:15 -bgc:base-2">B</div>
      <div class="l--box -p:15">Lorem ipsum</div>
      <div class="l--box -p:15">
        <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit, amet...</p>
      </div>
      <div class="l--box -p:15">Dolor sit amet</div>
      <div class="l--box -p:15">
        <p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit, amet...</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    ```

## `u--clipText`

A class for clipping a background with text.

<SrcCode path="src/scss/utility/_clipText.scss" />

  <PreviewTitle>Background clipped by text</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <Center>
      <Box util="clipText" bgr="no-repeat" bgi="linear-gradient(45deg, var(--blue), var(--pink))">
        <Text fz="5xl" fw="bold" hl="0" lts="l">TEXT</Text>
      </Box>
    </Center>
  <PreviewCode label="JSX" slot="tab">
    ```jsx
    <Center>
      <Box util="clipText" bgi="linear-gradient(45deg, var(--blue), var(--pink))">
        <Text fz="5xl" fw="bold" hl="0" lts="l">
          TEXT
        </Text>
      </Box>
    </Center>
    ```
  <PreviewCode label="HTML" slot="tab">
    ```html
    <div class="l--box u--clipText -bgi:linear-gradient(to top, #a8edea 0%, #fed6e3 100%)"></div>
    ```

## Opt-in

These utility classes are not included in the Lism CSS core stylesheet, but they are useful patterns you can add yourself.

### `u--inlineCenter`

A class for aligning emoji or inline icons to the vertical center of surrounding text.
Since `vertical-align: middle;` alone can cause misalignment, an additional `translate` adjustment is applied.

<Preview css={`
.u--inlineCenter {
  vertical-align: middle;
  translate: 0 calc(-1 * (0.35em - 0.5ex));
}`}>
  <PreviewTitle>Usage example</PreviewTitle>
  <PreviewArea p="20">
    <p>
      <Icon util="inlineCenter" icon="alert" c="red" fz="xl" /> Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.
    </p>
    <p>
      <Icon util="inlineCenter" as={Dog} fz="l" />
      Dog, and <Icon util="inlineCenter" as={Cat} fz="l" />
      Cat.
    </p>
    <p>
      <span class="u--inlineCenter -fz:xl">🚀</span> Emoji.
    </p>
    <p>
      <Icon fz="2xl" util="inlineCenter" src="https://emojix.s3.ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com/g3/svg/1f916.svg" alt="image" /> Inline img icon.
    </p>
    ```jsx "u--inlineCenter"
    <p><Icon util="inlineCenter" icon="alert" c="red" fz="xl" /> Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.</p>
    <p><Icon util="inlineCenter" as={Dog} fz="l" />Dog, and <Icon util="inlineCenter" as={Cat} fz="l"/>Cat.</p>
    <p><span class="u--inlineCenter -fz:xl">🚀</span> Emoji.</p>
    <p><Icon fz="2xl" util="inlineCenter" src="https://emojix.s3.ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com/g3/svg/1f916.svg" alt="image" /> Inline img icon.</p>
    ```

  <PreviewCode slot="tab" label="**Additional CSS**">
  ```css
  .u--inlineCenter {
    vertical-align: middle; /* Set baseline to middle */
    translate: 0 calc(-1 * (0.35em - 0.5ex)); /* Fine-tune based on the middle calculation. (0.5cap - 0.5ex is ideal for Latin text.) */
  }
  ```
